// database/seeders/default-data.seeder.ts
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { Permission } from '../entities/permission.entity';
import { Role } from '../entities/role.entity';
import { Company } from '../entities/company.entity';

export class DefaultDataSeeder {
  constructor(private dataSource: DataSource) {}

  async run(): Promise<void> {
    await this.seedPermissions();
    await this.seedRoles();
    await this.seedDefaultCompany();
  }

  private async seedPermissions(): Promise<void> {
    const permissionRepository = this.dataSource.getRepository(Permission);
    
    const permissions = [
      // User permissions
      { name: 'users:create', resource: 'users', action: 'create', description: 'Create new users' },
      { name: 'users:read', resource: 'users', action: 'read', description: 'View user information' },
      { name: 'users:update', resource: 'users', action: 'update', description: 'Update user information' },
      { name: 'users:delete', resource: 'users', action: 'delete', description: 'Delete users' },
      
      // Order permissions
      { name: 'orders:create', resource: 'orders', action: 'create', description: 'Create new orders' },
      { name: 'orders:read', resource: 'orders', action: 'read', description: 'View orders' },
      { name: 'orders:update', resource: 'orders', action: 'update', description: 'Update orders' },
      { name: 'orders:cancel', resource: 'orders', action: 'cancel', description: 'Cancel orders' },
      { name: 'orders:delete', resource: 'orders', action: 'delete', description: 'Delete orders' },
      
      // Product permissions
      { name: 'products:create', resource: 'products', action: 'create', description: 'Create new products' },
      { name: 'products:read', resource: 'products', action: 'read', description: 'View products' },
      { name: 'products:update', resource: 'products', action: 'update', description: 'Update products' },
      { name: 'products:delete', resource: 'products', action: 'delete', description: 'Delete products' },
      
      // Company permissions
      { name: 'companies:create', resource: 'companies', action: 'create', description: 'Create companies' },
      { name: 'companies:read', resource: 'companies', action: 'read', description: 'View companies' },
      { name: 'companies:update', resource: 'companies', action: 'update', description: 'Update companies' },
      { name: 'companies:delete', resource: 'companies', action: 'delete', description: 'Delete companies' },
    ];

    for (const permData of permissions) {
      const exists = await permissionRepository.findOne({ where: { name: permData.name } });
      if (!exists) {
        const permission = permissionRepository.create(permData);
        await permissionRepository.save(permission);
      }
    }
  }

  private async seedRoles(): Promise<void> {
    const roleRepository = this.dataSource.getRepository(Role);
    const permissionRepository = this.dataSource.getRepository(Permission);

    // Super Admin role
    const adminPermissions = await permissionRepository.find();
    let adminRole = await roleRepository.findOne({ 
      where: { name: 'SUPER_ADMIN' },
      relations: ['permissions']
    });
    
    if (!adminRole) {
      adminRole = roleRepository.create({
        name: 'SUPER_ADMIN',
        description: 'Super administrator with all permissions',
        permissions: adminPermissions,
      });
      await roleRepository.save(adminRole);
    }

    // Regular user role
    const userPermissions = await permissionRepository.find({
      where: [
        { name: 'orders:create' },
        { name: 'orders:read' },
        { name: 'orders:cancel' },
        { name: 'products:read' },
      ]
    });

    let userRole = await roleRepository.findOne({ 
      where: { name: 'USER' },
      relations: ['permissions']
    });
    
    if (!userRole) {
      userRole = roleRepository.create({
        name: 'USER',
        description: 'Regular user with basic permissions',
        permissions: userPermissions,
      });
      await roleRepository.save(userRole);
    }
  }

  private async seedDefaultCompany(): Promise<void> {
    const companyRepository = this.dataSource.getRepository(Company);
    
    const exists = await companyRepository.findOne({ where: { name: 'Default Company' } });
    if (!exists) {
      const company = companyRepository.create({
        name: 'Default Company',
        domain: 'default.com',
      });
      await companyRepository.save(company);
    }
  }
}

#!/bin/bash
# scripts/deploy.sh

set -e

PROJECT_ID=${1:-"your-gcp-project-id"}
REGION=${2:-"us-central1"}
CLUSTER_NAME=${3:-"ecommerce-cluster"}

echo "Deploying to GCP Project: $PROJECT_ID"
echo "Region: $REGION"
echo "Cluster: $CLUSTER_NAME"

# Build and push Docker images
echo "Building and pushing Docker images..."
docker build -t gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/auth-service:latest -f docker/auth-service.Dockerfile .
docker build -t gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/api-gateway:latest -f docker/api-gateway.Dockerfile .
docker build -t gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/user-service:latest -f docker/user-service.Dockerfile .
docker build -t gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/order-service:latest -f docker/order-service.Dockerfile .
docker build -t gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/product-service:latest -f docker/product-service.Dockerfile .

docker push gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/auth-service:latest
docker push gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/api-gateway:latest
docker push gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/user-service:latest
docker push gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/order-service:latest
docker push gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/product-service:latest

# Get GKE credentials
echo "Getting GKE credentials..."
gcloud container clusters get-credentials $CLUSTER_NAME --region=$REGION --project=$PROJECT_ID

# Apply Kubernetes manifests
echo "Applying Kubernetes manifests..."
kubectl apply -f k8s/namespace.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/rbac.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/configmap.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/secrets.yaml

# Deploy services
kubectl apply -f k8s/auth-service.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/api-gateway.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/user-service.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/order-service.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/product-service.yaml

# Apply Istio configurations
echo "Applying Istio configurations..."
kubectl apply -f k8s/istio/

echo "Waiting for deployments to be ready..."
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=600s deployment/auth-service -n ecommerce
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=600s deployment/api-gateway -n ecommerce
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=600s deployment/user-service -n ecommerce
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=600s deployment/order-service -n ecommerce
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=600s deployment/product-service -n ecommerce

echo "Deployment completed successfully!"
echo "API Gateway endpoint:"
kubectl get service api-gateway -n ecommerce -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}'

Security Best Practices Summary​

1. Authentication Security​

  • Use strong JWT secrets stored in Kubernetes secrets
  • Implement proper token expiration and rotation
  • Use bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds for password hashing
  • Implement account lockout after failed login attempts

2. Authorization Security​

  • Implement defense in depth with multiple authorization layers
  • Use principle of least privilege for role assignments
  • Validate resource ownership at the service level
  • Implement audit logging for all authorization decisions

3. Infrastructure Security​

  • Use Kubernetes RBAC for service account permissions
  • Implement network policies to restrict inter-service communication
  • Use Istio service mesh for mTLS between services
  • Store sensitive data in GCP Secret Manager or Kubernetes secrets

4. API Security​

  • Implement rate limiting at the API gateway level
  • Use HTTPS/TLS for all external communication
  • Validate all input data with proper sanitization
  • Implement proper CORS policies

5. Container Security​

  • Run containers as non-root users
  • Use read-only root filesystems
  • Implement resource limits and requests
  • Regularly scan container images for vulnerabilities

6. Monitoring and Observability​

  • Implement comprehensive logging for security events
  • Set up monitoring for failed authentication attempts
  • Use distributed tracing for request flow analysis
  • Implement alerting for suspicious activities

Conclusion​

This comprehensive implementation demonstrates how to build secure, scalable microservices with NestJS on GCP Kubernetes. The architecture incorporates:

  • Multi-layered Security: Authentication at the gateway, authorization at the service level
  • Enterprise Patterns: RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC authorization models
  • Cloud-Native Features: Kubernetes-native security, Istio service mesh, GCP integrations
  • Production Readiness: Proper error handling, monitoring, and deployment automation

Key benefits of this approach:

  1. Scalability: Each service can scale independently based on demand
  2. Security: Multiple layers of security from infrastructure to application level
  3. Maintainability: Clear separation of concerns and modular architecture
  4. Observability: Comprehensive logging, monitoring, and tracing
  5. Reliability: Health checks, circuit breakers, and proper error handling

This implementation provides a solid foundation for building enterprise-grade microservices with robust authentication and authorization mechanisms suitable for production deployment on Google Cloud Platform.

Further Resources​

  • NestJS Documentation
  • Kubernetes Security Best Practices
  • Istio Security Documentation
  • Google Cloud Security Best Practices
  • Microservices Security Patterns

Have you implemented similar microservices architectures? Share your experiences with authentication and authorization patterns in the comments!

item.title: Nginx: The High-Performance Web Server and Reverse Proxy
item.description: Nginx (pronounced "engine-x") is one of the most popular and powerful web servers in the world, powering over 30% of all websites on the internet. Originally created by Igor Sysoev in 2004 to solve the C10K problem (handling 10,000 concurrent connections), Nginx has evolved into a versatile tool that serves as a web server, reverse proxy, load balancer, and HTTP cache.
item.content:encoded:
Nginx (pronounced "engine-x") is one of the most popular and powerful web servers in the world, powering over 30% of all websites on the internet. Originally created by Igor Sysoev in 2004 to solve the C10K problem (handling 10,000 concurrent connections), Nginx has evolved into a versatile tool that serves as a web server, reverse proxy, load balancer, and HTTP cache.

In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore what makes Nginx special, its key features, common use cases, and how to get started with basic configurations.

What is Nginx?​

Nginx is an open-source web server that can also function as a reverse proxy, load balancer, mail proxy, and HTTP cache. Unlike traditional web servers that create a new thread or process for each request, Nginx uses an event-driven, asynchronous architecture that allows it to handle thousands of concurrent connections with minimal resource usage.

Key Characteristics​

  • High Performance: Handles thousands of concurrent connections efficiently
  • Low Memory Usage: Uses significantly less memory compared to Apache
  • Event-Driven Architecture: Non-blocking I/O operations
  • Modular Design: Extensible through modules
  • Configuration Flexibility: Simple yet powerful configuration syntax

Core Features​

1. Web Server​

Nginx can serve static content (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images) extremely efficiently. Its ability to handle static files makes it an excellent choice for serving modern web applications.

2. Reverse Proxy​

Acts as an intermediary between clients and backend servers, forwarding client requests to appropriate backend services and returning responses back to clients.

3. Load Balancing​

Distributes incoming requests across multiple backend servers to ensure optimal resource utilization and prevent any single server from becoming overwhelmed.

4. SSL/TLS Termination​

Handles SSL/TLS encryption and decryption, offloading this computationally intensive task from backend servers.

5. Caching​

Provides HTTP caching capabilities to store frequently requested content, reducing load on backend servers and improving response times.

Common Use Cases​

1. Static File Serving​

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name example.com;
    root /var/www/html;
    
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
    
    location ~* \.(jpg|jpeg|png|gif|ico|css|js)$ {
        expires 1y;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
    }
}

2. Reverse Proxy for Node.js Applications​

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name api.example.com;
    
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://localhost:3000;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection 'upgrade';
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
        proxy_cache_bypass $http_upgrade;
    }
}

3. Load Balancing​

upstream backend {
    server backend1.example.com;
    server backend2.example.com;
    server backend3.example.com;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name example.com;
    
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://backend;
    }
}

4. SSL/HTTPS Configuration​

server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name example.com;
    
    ssl_certificate /path/to/certificate.crt;
    ssl_certificate_key /path/to/private.key;
    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
    ssl_ciphers ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384;
    
    location / {
        root /var/www/html;
        index index.html;
    }
}

# Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name example.com;
    return 301 https://$server_name$request_uri;
}

Nginx vs Apache​

FeatureNginxApache
ArchitectureEvent-driven, asynchronousProcess/thread-based
Memory UsageLowerHigher
Static ContentExcellent performanceGood performance
ConfigurationCentralized config files.htaccess + main config
ModulesDynamic loadingBoth static and dynamic
Learning CurveModerateEasier for beginners

Installation and Basic Setup​

Ubuntu/Debian​

sudo apt update
sudo apt install nginx
sudo systemctl start nginx
sudo systemctl enable nginx

CentOS/RHEL​

sudo yum install epel-release
sudo yum install nginx
sudo systemctl start nginx
sudo systemctl enable nginx

macOS (with Homebrew)​

brew install nginx
brew services start nginx

macOS M4 Chip Specific Setup​

For Apple Silicon M4 processors, you may need to install Homebrew for ARM64 architecture if not already done:

# Install Homebrew (if not already installed)
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

# Ensure you're using ARM64 architecture
arch
# Should output: arm64

# Install Nginx optimized for M4
brew install nginx

# Verify installation and architecture
file $(brew --prefix)/bin/nginx
# Should show: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64

# Start Nginx with optimized settings for M4
brew services start nginx

# Check if running
brew services list | grep nginx

M4-Optimized Configuration​

For optimal performance on M4 chips, consider these configuration adjustments:

# /opt/homebrew/etc/nginx/nginx.conf (M4 optimized)
user _www;
worker_processes auto;  # M4 has efficient cores, auto-detection works well
error_log /opt/homebrew/var/log/nginx/error.log;

events {
    worker_connections 2048;  # M4 can handle higher connections efficiently
    use kqueue;  # Optimal for macOS
    multi_accept on;
}

http {
    include       mime.types;
    default_type  application/octet-stream;
    
    # M4 optimization settings
    sendfile on;
    tcp_nopush on;
    tcp_nodelay on;
    
    # Buffer sizes optimized for M4 memory bandwidth
    client_body_buffer_size 128k;
    client_max_body_size 10m;
    client_header_buffer_size 1k;
    large_client_header_buffers 4 4k;
    output_buffers 1 32k;
    postpone_output 1460;
    
    server {
        listen 8080;  # Default Homebrew port
        server_name localhost;
        root /opt/homebrew/var/www;
        index index.html index.htm;
        
        location / {
            try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
        }
    }
}

Common M4 Considerations​

  1. File Paths: Homebrew on M4 installs to /opt/homebrew/ instead of /usr/local/
  2. Default Port: Homebrew Nginx typically runs on port 8080 to avoid permission issues
  3. Process Management: Use brew services for better integration with macOS
  4. Performance: M4's efficiency cores handle Nginx's event-driven architecture exceptionally well
# M4-specific paths
Configuration: /opt/homebrew/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
Document root: /opt/homebrew/var/www
Error log: /opt/homebrew/var/log/nginx/error.log
Access log: /opt/homebrew/var/log/nginx/access.log

Basic Configuration Structure​

Nginx configuration is typically located at /etc/nginx/nginx.conf and follows a hierarchical structure:

# Main context
user nginx;
worker_processes auto;
error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log;

# Events context
events {
    worker_connections 1024;
}

# HTTP context
http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream;
    
    # Server context
    server {
        listen 80;
        server_name example.com;
        
        # Location context
        location / {
            root /var/www/html;
            index index.html;
        }
    }
}

Performance Optimization Tips​

1. Worker Processes​

Set worker processes to match your CPU cores:

worker_processes auto;

2. Worker Connections​

Increase worker connections for high-traffic sites:

events {
    worker_connections 2048;
    use epoll; # Linux
    use kqueue; # macOS/BSD
}

4. Gzip Compression​

Enable compression to reduce bandwidth:

gzip on;
gzip_vary on;
gzip_min_length 1024;
gzip_types text/plain text/css application/json application/javascript text/xml application/xml;

# M4 optimization: Use higher compression for better CPU/bandwidth trade-off
gzip_comp_level 6;  # M4 can handle higher compression efficiently
gzip_proxied any;

5. Browser Caching​

Set appropriate cache headers:

location ~* \.(jpg|jpeg|png|gif|ico|css|js)$ {
    expires 1y;
    add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
}

Security Best Practices​

1. Hide Nginx Version​

server_tokens off;

2. Rate Limiting​

# Basic rate limiting by IP address
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;

# Rate limiting by user session (requires session ID)
limit_req_zone $cookie_sessionid zone=session:10m rate=5r/s;

# Rate limiting by server name (per domain)
limit_req_zone $server_name zone=domain:10m rate=100r/s;

# Rate limiting by request URI (specific endpoints)
limit_req_zone $request_uri zone=endpoint:10m rate=2r/s;

# Whitelist trusted IPs
geo $limit {
    default 1;
    10.0.0.0/8 0;     # Internal network
    192.168.0.0/16 0; # Private network
    127.0.0.1/32 0;   # Localhost
}

map $limit $limit_key {
    0 "";
    1 $binary_remote_addr;
}

limit_req_zone $limit_key zone=trusted:10m rate=20r/s;

# Different rate limits for different locations
location /api/ {
    limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
    limit_req_status 429;
    limit_req_log_level warn;
}

location /login {
    # Stricter rate limiting for login attempts
    limit_req zone=api burst=5 nodelay;
    limit_req_status 429;
}

location /search {
    # Higher burst for search with delay
    limit_req zone=api burst=50;
}

location /upload {
    # Very strict rate limiting for uploads
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=upload:10m rate=1r/m;
    limit_req zone=upload burst=2;
}

location /public/ {
    # Use trusted zone for public content
    limit_req zone=trusted burst=100 nodelay;
}

Advanced Rate Limiting Configurations​

Multiple Rate Limits:

# Apply multiple rate limits simultaneously
location /api/critical/ {
    limit_req zone=api burst=10 nodelay;
    limit_req zone=session burst=5 nodelay;
    limit_req zone=endpoint burst=2 nodelay;
}

Dynamic Rate Limiting Based on Response Status:

# Stricter limits after failed attempts
map $status $loggable {
    ~^[23] 0;  # Don't log successful requests
    default 1;
}

limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=strict:10m rate=1r/s;

location /api/auth {
    limit_req zone=api burst=10;
    
    # Apply stricter limits if previous requests failed
    if ($http_x_failed_attempts) {
        limit_req zone=strict burst=3;
    }
}

Rate Limiting with Custom Error Pages:

# Custom error page for rate limited requests
error_page 429 /rate_limit.html;

location = /rate_limit.html {
    root /var/www/error;
    internal;
    add_header Content-Type text/html;
    add_header Retry-After 60;
}

location /api/ {
    limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
    limit_req_status 429;
}

Burst Control Strategies:

# No burst - strict limiting
location /strict-api/ {
    limit_req zone=api;
}

# Burst with delay - smoother for users
location /smooth-api/ {
    limit_req zone=api burst=10;
}

# Burst with nodelay - fast response but strict enforcement
location /fast-api/ {
    limit_req zone=api burst=10 nodelay;
}

3. Security Headers​

add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;
add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
add_header Referrer-Policy "no-referrer-when-downgrade" always;
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'" always;

Comprehensive Security Headers Explained​

X-Frame-Options - Prevents Clickjacking Attacks:

# DENY: Prevents any domain from framing the content
add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;

# SAMEORIGIN: Only allows framing from the same origin
add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;

# ALLOW-FROM: Allows framing from specific domains
add_header X-Frame-Options "ALLOW-FROM https://trusted-site.com" always;

Content-Security-Policy (CSP) - Prevents XSS and Data Injection:

# Basic CSP - only allow resources from same origin
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'" always;

# Advanced CSP for modern web applications
add_header Content-Security-Policy "
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net https://ajax.googleapis.com;
    style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com;
    font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com;
    img-src 'self' data: https:;
    connect-src 'self' https://api.example.com;
    frame-ancestors 'none';
    base-uri 'self';
    form-action 'self';
    upgrade-insecure-requests;
" always;

# CSP for Single Page Applications (React/Vue/Angular)
add_header Content-Security-Policy "
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' 'sha256-xyz123...' 'unsafe-eval';
    style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
    img-src 'self' data: blob: https:;
    font-src 'self' data:;
    connect-src 'self' wss: https:;
    worker-src 'self' blob:;
" always;

Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) - Enforces HTTPS:

# Basic HSTS - 1 year, include subdomains
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;

# HSTS with preload (for submission to browsers' preload lists)
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;

# Development/staging environment (shorter duration)
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=300; includeSubDomains" always;

X-Content-Type-Options - Prevents MIME Type Sniffing:

# Prevents browsers from interpreting files as different MIME types
add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;

Referrer-Policy - Controls Referrer Information:

# No referrer when protocol security is downgraded
add_header Referrer-Policy "no-referrer-when-downgrade" always;

# Strict referrer policy options
add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
add_header Referrer-Policy "same-origin" always;
add_header Referrer-Policy "no-referrer" always;

# Origin only (no path information)
add_header Referrer-Policy "origin" always;

X-XSS-Protection - Legacy XSS Protection:

# Enable XSS filtering and block page rendering if attack detected
add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;

# Note: This header is largely deprecated in favor of CSP
# Modern browsers rely on Content-Security-Policy instead

Permissions-Policy - Controls Browser Features:

# Disable potentially dangerous features
add_header Permissions-Policy "
    camera=(),
    microphone=(),
    geolocation=(),
    payment=(),
    usb=(),
    magnetometer=(),
    gyroscope=(),
    speaker=()
" always;

# Allow specific features for your domain only
add_header Permissions-Policy "
    camera=(self),
    microphone=(self),
    geolocation=(self 'https://trusted-maps.com'),
    payment=(self)
" always;

Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy & Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy:

# Enable cross-origin isolation for advanced features
add_header Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy "require-corp" always;
add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin" always;

# More permissive options
add_header Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy "credentialless" always;
add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin-allow-popups" always;

Complete Security Headers Configuration​

Production-Ready Security Headers Set:

# Complete security headers configuration
location / {
    # HSTS - Force HTTPS for 1 year
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;
    
    # Prevent clickjacking
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
    
    # Prevent MIME type sniffing
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
    
    # Control referrer information
    add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
    
    # Comprehensive CSP
    add_header Content-Security-Policy "
        default-src 'self';
        script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net;
        style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com;
        font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com;
        img-src 'self' data: https:;
        connect-src 'self' https:;
        frame-ancestors 'none';
        base-uri 'self';
        form-action 'self';
        upgrade-insecure-requests;
    " always;
    
    # Control browser features
    add_header Permissions-Policy "
        camera=(),
        microphone=(),
        geolocation=(),
        payment=(),
        usb=()
    " always;
    
    # Cross-origin policies
    add_header Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy "credentialless" always;
    add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin-allow-popups" always;
    
    # Remove server information
    add_header X-Powered-By "" always;
    
    # Custom security headers
    add_header X-Robots-Tag "noindex, nofollow" always;  # For admin areas
    add_header Cache-Control "no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate" always;  # For sensitive pages
}

Environment-Specific Configurations​

Development Environment:

# Relaxed headers for development
add_header Content-Security-Policy "
    default-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval';
    connect-src 'self' ws: wss: http: https:;
" always;

add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=300" always;  # Short duration

API Endpoints:

location /api/ {
    # API-specific security headers
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
    add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;
    add_header Cache-Control "no-store" always;
    add_header Pragma "no-cache" always;
    
    # CORS headers (if needed)
    add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin "https://yourdomain.com" always;
    add_header Access-Control-Allow-Methods "GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS" always;
    add_header Access-Control-Allow-Headers "Authorization, Content-Type" always;
    add_header Access-Control-Max-Age "86400" always;
}

Static Assets:

location ~* \.(js|css|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|ico|svg|woff|woff2)$ {
    # Relaxed CSP for static assets
    add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'" always;
    add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" always;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
}

Security Headers Testing and Validation​

Tools for Testing Security Headers:

  • Security Headers Scanner
  • Mozilla Observatory
  • OWASP ZAP

Common CSP Testing:

# Report-only mode for testing CSP before enforcement
add_header Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only "
    default-src 'self';
    report-uri /csp-report;
" always;

# CSP violation reporting endpoint
location /csp-report {
    access_log /var/log/nginx/csp-violations.log;
    return 204;
}

Modern Web Development with Nginx​

Microservices Architecture​

Nginx excels in microservices environments, routing requests to different services based on URL patterns:

location /auth/ {
    proxy_pass http://auth-service:3001/;
}

location /users/ {
    proxy_pass http://user-service:3002/;
}

location /orders/ {
    proxy_pass http://order-service:3003/;
}

API Gateway​

Use Nginx as an API gateway for request routing, authentication, and rate limiting:

location /api/v1/ {
    auth_request /auth;
    proxy_pass http://api-backend/;
}

location = /auth {
    internal;
    proxy_pass http://auth-service/verify;
    proxy_pass_request_body off;
    proxy_set_header Content-Length "";
    proxy_set_header X-Original-URI $request_uri;
}

Monitoring and Logging​

Access Logs​

log_format main '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" '
                '$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" '
                '"$http_user_agent" "$http_x_forwarded_for"';

access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;

Error Logs​

error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log warn;

Status Module​

Enable the status module for monitoring:

location /nginx_status {
    stub_status on;
    access_log off;
    allow 127.0.0.1;
    deny all;
}

Conclusion​

Nginx has proven itself as an indispensable tool in modern web infrastructure. Its performance, flexibility, and rich feature set make it suitable for everything from simple static websites to complex, high-traffic applications. Whether you're serving static content, implementing a reverse proxy, or building a sophisticated load balancing solution, Nginx provides the tools and performance you need.

As web applications continue to evolve, Nginx remains at the forefront, adapting to new requirements while maintaining its core strengths: high performance, low resource usage, and exceptional reliability.

Further Reading​

  • Official Nginx Documentation
  • Nginx Admin Guide
  • Let's Encrypt with Nginx
  • Nginx Performance Tuning

Have you used Nginx in your projects? Share your experiences and configurations in the comments below!

item.title: The Art of Prompt Engineering: How to Create Effective Prompts for AI
item.description: Prompt engineering has become one of the most crucial skills in the age of large language models (LLMs). Whether you're using ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or any other AI model, the quality of your prompts directly determines the quality of the responses you get. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore the best practices for creating effective prompts that consistently deliver high-quality results.
item.content:encoded:
Prompt engineering has become one of the most crucial skills in the age of large language models (LLMs). Whether you're using ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or any other AI model, the quality of your prompts directly determines the quality of the responses you get. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore the best practices for creating effective prompts that consistently deliver high-quality results.

Understanding how to craft good prompts is like learning to communicate effectively with a highly knowledgeable but literal-minded assistant. The better your instructions, the better the outcomes.

What is Prompt Engineering?​

Prompt engineering is the practice of designing and optimizing text inputs (prompts) to elicit the best possible responses from AI language models. It's both an art and a science that involves understanding how these models interpret and respond to different types of instructions.

Think of it as writing clear, specific instructions for a very capable but literal assistant. The assistant can perform complex tasks, but only if you communicate your needs effectively.

Why Good Prompts Matter​

The difference between a poorly crafted prompt and a well-engineered one can be dramatic:

  • Poor prompt: "Tell me about Earth"
  • Good prompt: "Generate a list of ways that makes Earth unique compared to other planets"

The first might give you a generic encyclopedia entry, while the second will provide focused, valuable insights tailored to your specific need.

Core Principles of Effective Prompt Engineering​

1. Be Concise​

The Problem: Verbose prompts introduce unnecessary noise that can confuse the model and dilute your intent.

❌ Not Recommended:

What do you think could be a good name for a flower shop that 
specializes in selling bouquets of dried flowers more than fresh flowers?

✅ Recommended:

Suggest a name for a flower shop that sells bouquets of dried flowers

Why it works: The concise version eliminates unnecessary words while preserving the core request. The model can focus on the essential task without getting distracted by conversational filler.

2. Be Specific and Well-Defined​

Vague prompts lead to vague responses. The more specific you are about what you want, the more targeted the response will be.

❌ Too Generic:

Tell me about Earth

✅ Specific and Targeted:

Generate a list of ways that makes Earth unique compared to other planets

The difference: The specific prompt gives the model a clear framework (comparison with other planets) and a specific output format (a list), resulting in a much more useful response.

3. Ask One Task at a Time​

Multi-part questions often lead to incomplete or imbalanced responses where one part gets more attention than others.

❌ Multiple Tasks:

What's the best method of boiling water and why is the sky blue?

✅ Single Task:

What's the best method of boiling water?

Then separately:

Why is the sky blue?

Benefits: Single-task prompts ensure each question gets the full attention it deserves and produces more thorough, focused responses.

Advanced Techniques​

Using System Instructions for Guardrails​

System instructions help prevent the AI from veering off-topic or providing inappropriate responses. They act as behavioral guidelines for the entire conversation.

Example Travel Chatbot System Instruction:

You are an AI chatbot for a travel website. Your mission is to provide 
helpful queries for travelers. Before answering any question, check if 
it complies with your mission. If not, respond with "Sorry, I can't 
answer that question."

This approach helps maintain focus and prevents the AI from responding to unrelated queries like cooking recipes when it should be helping with travel.

Turn Generative Tasks into Classification Tasks​

When you need more predictable, controlled outputs, convert open-ended questions into multiple-choice formats.

❌ High Variability (Generative):

I'm a high school student. Recommend me a programming activity to improve my skills.

✅ Lower Variability (Classification):

I'm a high school student. Which of these activities do you suggest and why:
a) learn Python
b) learn JavaScript  
c) learn Fortran

Why this works: Classification tasks constrain the possible outputs, making responses more predictable and easier to process programmatically.

The Power of Examples: Zero-Shot vs Few-Shot Prompting​

Zero-Shot Prompting​

Zero-shot prompting provides no examples, relying entirely on the model's training to understand the task.

Example:

Decide whether a Tweet's sentiment is positive, neutral, or negative.

Tweet: I loved the new YouTube video you made!
Sentiment:

One-Shot Prompting​

One-shot prompting provides a single example to guide the model's understanding.

Example:

Decide whether a Tweet's sentiment is positive, neutral, or negative.

Tweet: I loved the new YouTube video you made!
Sentiment: positive

Tweet: That was awful. Super boring 😠
Sentiment:

Few-Shot Prompting​

Few-shot prompting provides multiple examples to establish a clear pattern.

Example:

Decide whether a Tweet's sentiment is positive, neutral, or negative.

Tweet: I loved the new YouTube video you made!
Sentiment: positive

Tweet: That was awful. Super boring 😠
Sentiment: negative

Tweet: Something surprised me about this video - it was actually original. 
It was not the same old recycled stuff that I always see. Watch it - you will not regret it.
Sentiment:

When to Use Each Approach​

  • Zero-shot: When you want creative, open-ended responses
  • One-shot: When you need to establish a basic pattern or format
  • Few-shot: When you need consistent, predictable responses that follow a specific pattern

Dealing with Hallucinations​

AI models can generate confident-sounding but factually incorrect information, known as "hallucinations." Here's how to minimize them:

1. Be Aware of Knowledge Cutoffs​

❌ "What day is it today?"
✅ "What day of the week typically has the highest retail sales?"

2. Ask for Uncertainty Acknowledgment​

✅ "List the major causes of World War I. If you're uncertain about any point, please indicate that."

3. Request Sources (with caution)​

✅ "Explain photosynthesis and indicate which parts are well-established science versus current research areas."

Note: Asking for citations doesn't eliminate hallucinations, as models can fabricate sources too.

Industry-Specific Prompt Patterns​

For Code Generation​

Write a Python function that [specific task]. Include:
- Input validation
- Error handling  
- Type hints
- A docstring with usage examples

For Content Creation​

Write a [blog post/email/social media post] about [topic] that:
- Targets [specific audience]
- Has a [tone: professional/casual/friendly]
- Includes [specific elements]
- Is approximately [word count] words

For Data Analysis​

Analyze this data and provide:
1. Key trends and patterns
2. Notable outliers or anomalies  
3. Three actionable insights
4. Confidence level for each finding

[Insert data]

Testing and Iterating Your Prompts​

A/B Testing Approach​

  1. Create variations of your prompt
  2. Test with the same input multiple times
  3. Compare outputs for consistency and quality
  4. Refine based on results

Prompt Versioning​

Keep track of prompt variations and their performance:

v1.0: "Summarize this article"
v1.1: "Summarize this article in 3 bullet points"  
v1.2: "Summarize this article in 3 bullet points, focusing on key actions and outcomes"

Common Prompt Engineering Mistakes​

1. Over-Engineering​

Don't make prompts unnecessarily complex. Start simple and add complexity only when needed.

2. Assuming Human Context​

AI doesn't have access to your screen, previous conversations (unless explicitly provided), or real-time information.

3. Ignoring Model Limitations​

Each model has token limits, knowledge cutoffs, and specific strengths and weaknesses.

4. Not Testing Edge Cases​

Test your prompts with unusual inputs to understand their robustness.

Best Practices for Different Use Cases​

Creative Writing​

  • Use open-ended prompts
  • Provide style or tone guidance
  • Include creative constraints for more interesting outputs

Technical Documentation​

  • Be extremely specific about format
  • Include examples of desired output
  • Specify technical level for the audience

Customer Service​

  • Use system instructions for brand voice
  • Include escalation paths for complex issues
  • Test with challenging customer scenarios

Data Processing​

  • Provide clear input/output format specifications
  • Include error handling instructions
  • Test with edge cases and malformed data

Measuring Prompt Effectiveness​

Quantitative Metrics​

  • Consistency: How similar are responses to the same prompt?
  • Accuracy: How often are factual claims correct?
  • Relevance: How well does the output match the request?
  • Completeness: Does the response address all parts of the prompt?

Qualitative Assessment​

  • Usefulness: Does the output solve your problem?
  • Clarity: Is the response well-structured and understandable?
  • Tone: Does it match your desired communication style?

Tools and Resources for Prompt Engineering​

Prompt Libraries​

  • Keep successful prompts organized by use case
  • Document what works and what doesn't
  • Share effective prompts with your team

Testing Frameworks​

  • Use systematic approaches to test prompt variations
  • Automate testing where possible
  • Track performance over time

Community Resources​

  • Join prompt engineering communities
  • Study examples from others in your field
  • Contribute your own successful patterns

Future of Prompt Engineering​

As AI models continue to evolve, prompt engineering techniques will also advance:

Emerging Trends​

  • Multimodal prompts: Combining text, images, and other media
  • Chain-of-thought prompting: Breaking complex tasks into steps
  • Role-based prompting: Having the AI adopt specific personas or expertise
  • Meta-prompting: Using AI to help design better prompts

Skills to Develop​

  • Understanding model capabilities and limitations
  • Systematic testing and evaluation methods
  • Domain expertise to create relevant examples
  • Communication skills for clear instruction writing

Conclusion​

Effective prompt engineering is a crucial skill in our AI-powered world. By following these best practices—being concise, specific, and strategic about examples—you can dramatically improve the quality and consistency of AI-generated responses.

Remember that prompt engineering is both an art and a science. While these guidelines provide a solid foundation, the best prompts often come from experimentation, iteration, and deep understanding of your specific use case.

Key takeaways:

  • Start simple and add complexity gradually
  • Test thoroughly with various inputs and edge cases
  • Use examples strategically to guide model behavior
  • Be specific about format, tone, and requirements
  • Consider the model's limitations when designing prompts
  • Iterate based on results rather than assuming first attempts are optimal

As AI models become more sophisticated, the ability to communicate effectively with them will only become more valuable. Master these prompt engineering fundamentals, and you'll be well-equipped to leverage AI tools effectively in whatever domain you work in.

Further Reading​

  • Google's Prompt Design Guidelines
  • OpenAI's Prompt Engineering Guide
  • Anthropic's Prompt Engineering Guide
  • Best Practices for Prompt Engineering with OpenAI API

What prompt engineering techniques have worked best for you? Share your experiences and favorite patterns in the comments below!

item.title: Building an Interactive Tour Guide for New Features - Full-Stack Developer Guide
item.description: Creating an effective interactive tour guide is crucial for helping users discover and adopt new features in your application. A well-designed tour can significantly improve user onboarding, feature adoption rates, and overall user satisfaction. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore how to build a flexible, accessible, and engaging tour system that can highlight new features and guide users through complex workflows.
item.content:encoded:
Creating an effective interactive tour guide is crucial for helping users discover and adopt new features in your application. A well-designed tour can significantly improve user onboarding, feature adoption rates, and overall user satisfaction. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore how to build a flexible, accessible, and engaging tour system that can highlight new features and guide users through complex workflows.

Why Interactive Tours Matter​

Before diving into implementation, let's understand why interactive tours are essential for modern applications:

📈 Improved Feature Adoption​

  • New features often go unnoticed without proper introduction
  • Tours increase feature discovery by 40-60% on average
  • Guided experiences reduce the learning curve for complex features

🎯 Enhanced User Onboarding​

  • Contextual guidance reduces user frustration
  • Step-by-step walkthroughs improve task completion rates
  • Personalized tours adapt to different user roles and experience levels

💡 Reduced Support Burden​

  • Proactive guidance prevents common user questions
  • Self-service learning reduces support ticket volume
  • Interactive help is available exactly when needed

Tour System Architecture​

Let's build a tour system that's flexible, reusable, and easy to maintain. Our architecture will consist of several key components:

// Types for our tour system
interface TourStep {
  id: string;
  target: string; // CSS selector or element ID
  title: string;
  content: string;
  placement?: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'center';
  action?: 'click' | 'hover' | 'focus' | 'none';
  beforeShow?: () => Promise<void> | void;
  afterShow?: () => Promise<void> | void;
  beforeHide?: () => Promise<void> | void;
  skipable?: boolean;
  highlightPadding?: number;
  zIndex?: number;
}

interface Tour {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  description: string;
  steps: TourStep[];
  triggerConditions?: TriggerCondition[];
  userSegments?: string[];
  isActive: boolean;
  priority: number;
}

interface TourState {
  currentTour: Tour | null;
  currentStepIndex: number;
  isPlaying: boolean;
  completedTours: string[];
  skippedTours: string[];
}

Core Tour Engine Implementation​

Let's start with the main tour engine that will manage tour execution:

// hooks/useTourEngine.ts
import { useState, useEffect, useCallback, useRef } from 'react';
import { useLocalStorage } from './useLocalStorage';

export const useTourEngine = () => {
  const [tourState, setTourState] = useState<TourState>({
    currentTour: null,
    currentStepIndex: 0,
    isPlaying: false,
    completedTours: [],
    skippedTours: [],
  });

  const [completedTours, setCompletedTours] = useLocalStorage<string[]>('tour-completed', []);
  const [skippedTours, setSkippedTours] = useLocalStorage<string[]>('tour-skipped', []);
  
  const overlayRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
  const highlightRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);

  // Start a tour
  const startTour = useCallback(async (tour: Tour) => {
    if (completedTours.includes(tour.id) || skippedTours.includes(tour.id)) {
      return;
    }

    setTourState({
      currentTour: tour,
      currentStepIndex: 0,
      isPlaying: true,
      completedTours,
      skippedTours,
    });

    // Execute beforeShow hook for first step
    if (tour.steps[0]?.beforeShow) {
      await tour.steps[0].beforeShow();
    }
  }, [completedTours, skippedTours]);

  // Navigate to next step
  const nextStep = useCallback(async () => {
    if (!tourState.currentTour) return;

    const currentStep = tourState.currentTour.steps[tourState.currentStepIndex];
    
    // Execute beforeHide hook
    if (currentStep?.beforeHide) {
      await currentStep.beforeHide();
    }

    const nextIndex = tourState.currentStepIndex + 1;
    
    if (nextIndex >= tourState.currentTour.steps.length) {
      // Tour completed
      completeTour();
      return;
    }

    setTourState(prev => ({
      ...prev,
      currentStepIndex: nextIndex,
    }));

    // Execute beforeShow hook for next step
    const nextStep = tourState.currentTour.steps[nextIndex];
    if (nextStep?.beforeShow) {
      await nextStep.beforeShow();
    }
  }, [tourState]);

  // Navigate to previous step
  const previousStep = useCallback(async () => {
    if (!tourState.currentTour || tourState.currentStepIndex === 0) return;

    const currentStep = tourState.currentTour.steps[tourState.currentStepIndex];
    
    if (currentStep?.beforeHide) {
      await currentStep.beforeHide();
    }

    const prevIndex = tourState.currentStepIndex - 1;
    setTourState(prev => ({
      ...prev,
      currentStepIndex: prevIndex,
    }));

    const prevStep = tourState.currentTour.steps[prevIndex];
    if (prevStep?.beforeShow) {
      await prevStep.beforeShow();
    }
  }, [tourState]);

  // Complete tour
  const completeTour = useCallback(() => {
    if (!tourState.currentTour) return;

    const newCompleted = [...completedTours, tourState.currentTour.id];
    setCompletedTours(newCompleted);
    
    setTourState(prev => ({
      ...prev,
      currentTour: null,
      currentStepIndex: 0,
      isPlaying: false,
      completedTours: newCompleted,
    }));
  }, [tourState.currentTour, completedTours, setCompletedTours]);

  // Skip tour
  const skipTour = useCallback(() => {
    if (!tourState.currentTour) return;

    const newSkipped = [...skippedTours, tourState.currentTour.id];
    setSkippedTours(newSkipped);
    
    setTourState(prev => ({
      ...prev,
      currentTour: null,
      currentStepIndex: 0,
      isPlaying: false,
      skippedTours: newSkipped,
    }));
  }, [tourState.currentTour, skippedTours, setSkippedTours]);

  // Get current step
  const getCurrentStep = useCallback((): TourStep | null => {
    if (!tourState.currentTour) return null;
    return tourState.currentTour.steps[tourState.currentStepIndex] || null;
  }, [tourState]);

  return {
    tourState,
    startTour,
    nextStep,
    previousStep,
    completeTour,
    skipTour,
    getCurrentStep,
  };
};

Tour Overlay Component​

The overlay component creates the spotlight effect and manages the visual presentation:

// components/TourOverlay/TourOverlay.tsx
import React, { useEffect, useState, useRef } from 'react';
import { createPortal } from 'react-dom';
import { TourStep } from '../../types/tour.types';
import { TourTooltip } from './TourTooltip';

interface TourOverlayProps {
  step: TourStep;
  onNext: () => void;
  onPrevious: () => void;
  onSkip: () => void;
  onComplete: () => void;
  currentStepIndex: number;
  totalSteps: number;
  isFirstStep: boolean;
  isLastStep: boolean;
}

export const TourOverlay: React.FC<TourOverlayProps> = ({
  step,
  onNext,
  onPrevious,
  onSkip,
  onComplete,
  currentStepIndex,
  totalSteps,
  isFirstStep,
  isLastStep,
}) => {
  const [targetElement, setTargetElement] = useState<HTMLElement | null>(null);
  const [targetRect, setTargetRect] = useState<DOMRect | null>(null);
  const [tooltipPosition, setTooltipPosition] = useState({ x: 0, y: 0 });
  const overlayRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const element = document.querySelector(step.target) as HTMLElement;
    if (element) {
      setTargetElement(element);
      updatePositions(element);
      
      // Scroll element into view
      element.scrollIntoView({
        behavior: 'smooth',
        block: 'center',
        inline: 'center',
      });

      // Add highlight class to target element
      element.classList.add('tour-highlight');
      
      // Execute step action
      if (step.action === 'click') {
        element.click();
      } else if (step.action === 'focus') {
        element.focus();
      } else if (step.action === 'hover') {
        element.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mouseenter', { bubbles: true }));
      }
    }

    return () => {
      if (element) {
        element.classList.remove('tour-highlight');
      }
    };
  }, [step]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleResize = () => {
      if (targetElement) {
        updatePositions(targetElement);
      }
    };

    const handleScroll = () => {
      if (targetElement) {
        updatePositions(targetElement);
      }
    };

    window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);
    window.addEventListener('scroll', handleScroll, true);

    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize);
      window.removeEventListener('scroll', handleScroll, true);
    };
  }, [targetElement]);

  const updatePositions = (element: HTMLElement) => {
    const rect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
    setTargetRect(rect);

    // Calculate tooltip position based on placement preference
    const placement = step.placement || 'bottom';
    const padding = step.highlightPadding || 8;
    
    let tooltipX = 0;
    let tooltipY = 0;

    switch (placement) {
      case 'top':
        tooltipX = rect.left + rect.width / 2;
        tooltipY = rect.top - padding;
        break;
      case 'bottom':
        tooltipX = rect.left + rect.width / 2;
        tooltipY = rect.bottom + padding;
        break;
      case 'left':
        tooltipX = rect.left - padding;
        tooltipY = rect.top + rect.height / 2;
        break;
      case 'right':
        tooltipX = rect.right + padding;
        tooltipY = rect.top + rect.height / 2;
        break;
      case 'center':
        tooltipX = window.innerWidth / 2;
        tooltipY = window.innerHeight / 2;
        break;
    }

    setTooltipPosition({ x: tooltipX, y: tooltipY });
  };

  const handleKeyDown = (e: React.KeyboardEvent) => {
    switch (e.key) {
      case 'Escape':
        onSkip();
        break;
      case 'ArrowRight':
      case 'Enter':
      case ' ':
        e.preventDefault();
        if (isLastStep) {
          onComplete();
        } else {
          onNext();
        }
        break;
      case 'ArrowLeft':
        e.preventDefault();
        if (!isFirstStep) {
          onPrevious();
        }
        break;
    }
  };

  if (!targetRect) return null;

  const overlayStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
    position: 'fixed',
    top: 0,
    left: 0,
    right: 0,
    bottom: 0,
    backgroundColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)',
    zIndex: step.zIndex || 1000,
    pointerEvents: 'auto',
  };

  const spotlightStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
    position: 'absolute',
    top: targetRect.top - (step.highlightPadding || 8),
    left: targetRect.left - (step.highlightPadding || 8),
    width: targetRect.width + (step.highlightPadding || 8) * 2,
    height: targetRect.height + (step.highlightPadding || 8) * 2,
    boxShadow: `0 0 0 9999px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`,
    borderRadius: '8px',
    pointerEvents: 'none',
  };

  return createPortal(
    <div
      ref={overlayRef}
      style={overlayStyle}
      onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
      tabIndex={-1}
      role="dialog"
      aria-modal="true"
      aria-labelledby="tour-title"
      aria-describedby="tour-content"
    >
      {/* Spotlight effect */}
      <div style={spotlightStyle} />
      
      {/* Tooltip */}
      <TourTooltip
        step={step}
        position={tooltipPosition}
        onNext={onNext}
        onPrevious={onPrevious}
        onSkip={onSkip}
        onComplete={onComplete}
        currentStepIndex={currentStepIndex}
        totalSteps={totalSteps}
        isFirstStep={isFirstStep}
        isLastStep={isLastStep}
        placement={step.placement || 'bottom'}
      />
    </div>,
    document.body
  );
};

Tour Tooltip Component​

The tooltip displays step content and navigation controls:

// components/TourOverlay/TourTooltip.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { TourStep } from '../../types/tour.types';

interface TourTooltipProps {
  step: TourStep;
  position: { x: number; y: number };
  placement: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'center';
  onNext: () => void;
  onPrevious: () => void;
  onSkip: () => void;
  onComplete: () => void;
  currentStepIndex: number;
  totalSteps: number;
  isFirstStep: boolean;
  isLastStep: boolean;
}

export const TourTooltip: React.FC<TourTooltipProps> = ({
  step,
  position,
  placement,
  onNext,
  onPrevious,
  onSkip,
  onComplete,
  currentStepIndex,
  totalSteps,
  isFirstStep,
  isLastStep,
}) => {
  const getTooltipStyle = (): React.CSSProperties => {
    const baseStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
      position: 'absolute',
      backgroundColor: 'white',
      borderRadius: '12px',
      padding: '20px',
      boxShadow: '0 10px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)',
      maxWidth: '320px',
      minWidth: '280px',
      zIndex: 1001,
      transform: getTransform(),
    };

    return {
      ...baseStyle,
      left: position.x,
      top: position.y,
    };
  };

  const getTransform = (): string => {
    switch (placement) {
      case 'top':
        return 'translate(-50%, -100%)';
      case 'bottom':
        return 'translate(-50%, 0)';
      case 'left':
        return 'translate(-100%, -50%)';
      case 'right':
        return 'translate(0, -50%)';
      case 'center':
        return 'translate(-50%, -50%)';
      default:
        return 'translate(-50%, 0)';
    }
  };

  const getArrowStyle = (): React.CSSProperties | null => {
    if (placement === 'center') return null;

    const baseArrow: React.CSSProperties = {
      position: 'absolute',
      width: 0,
      height: 0,
      borderStyle: 'solid',
    };

    switch (placement) {
      case 'top':
        return {
          ...baseArrow,
          bottom: '-8px',
          left: '50%',
          transform: 'translateX(-50%)',
          borderWidth: '8px 8px 0 8px',
          borderColor: 'white transparent transparent transparent',
        };
      case 'bottom':
        return {
          ...baseArrow,
          top: '-8px',
          left: '50%',
          transform: 'translateX(-50%)',
          borderWidth: '0 8px 8px 8px',
          borderColor: 'transparent transparent white transparent',
        };
      case 'left':
        return {
          ...baseArrow,
          right: '-8px',
          top: '50%',
          transform: 'translateY(-50%)',
          borderWidth: '8px 0 8px 8px',
          borderColor: 'transparent transparent transparent white',
        };
      case 'right':
        return {
          ...baseArrow,
          left: '-8px',
          top: '50%',
          transform: 'translateY(-50%)',
          borderWidth: '8px 8px 8px 0',
          borderColor: 'transparent white transparent transparent',
        };
      default:
        return null;
    }
  };

  return (
    <div style={getTooltipStyle()} className="tour-tooltip">
      {/* Arrow */}
      {getArrowStyle() && <div style={getArrowStyle()!} />}
      
      {/* Header */}
      <div className="tour-tooltip__header">
        <h3 id="tour-title" className="tour-tooltip__title">
          {step.title}
        </h3>
        <div className="tour-tooltip__progress">
          <span className="tour-tooltip__step-counter">
            {currentStepIndex + 1} of {totalSteps}
          </span>
          <div className="tour-tooltip__progress-bar">
            <div
              className="tour-tooltip__progress-fill"
              style={{
                width: `${((currentStepIndex + 1) / totalSteps) * 100}%`,
              }}
            />
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* Content */}
      <div
        id="tour-content"
        className="tour-tooltip__content"
        dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: step.content }}
      />

      {/* Navigation */}
      <div className="tour-tooltip__actions">
        <div className="tour-tooltip__actions-left">
          {step.skipable !== false && (
            <button
              onClick={onSkip}
              className="tour-button tour-button--secondary"
              type="button"
            >
              Skip Tour
            </button>
          )}
        </div>
        
        <div className="tour-tooltip__actions-right">
          {!isFirstStep && (
            <button
              onClick={onPrevious}
              className="tour-button tour-button--secondary"
              type="button"
            >
              Previous
            </button>
          )}
          
          <button
            onClick={isLastStep ? onComplete : onNext}
            className="tour-button tour-button--primary"
            type="button"
            autoFocus
          >
            {isLastStep ? 'Finish' : 'Next'}
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

Tour Manager for Multiple Tours​

A tour manager handles multiple tours and their triggering conditions:

// hooks/useTourManager.ts
import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';
import { Tour, TriggerCondition } from '../types/tour.types';
import { useTourEngine } from './useTourEngine';

interface TourManagerConfig {
  tours: Tour[];
  autoStart?: boolean;
  debugMode?: boolean;
}

export const useTourManager = ({ tours, autoStart = true, debugMode = false }: TourManagerConfig) => {
  const [availableTours, setAvailableTours] = useState<Tour[]>([]);
  const tourEngine = useTourEngine();

  // Evaluate tour trigger conditions
  const evaluateTriggerConditions = useCallback((conditions: TriggerCondition[]): boolean => {
    return conditions.every(condition => {
      switch (condition.type) {
        case 'url_match':
          return window.location.pathname.includes(condition.value);
        
        case 'element_exists':
          return document.querySelector(condition.value) !== null;
        
        case 'user_segment':
          // This would typically check against user data from your auth system
          const userSegment = localStorage.getItem('user_segment');
          return userSegment === condition.value;
        
        case 'feature_flag':
          // Check if a feature flag is enabled
          const featureFlags = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('feature_flags') || '{}');
          return featureFlags[condition.value] === true;
        
        case 'page_visit_count':
          const visitCount = parseInt(localStorage.getItem('page_visit_count') || '0');
          return visitCount >= parseInt(condition.value);
        
        case 'time_on_page':
          // This would need to be implemented with a timer
          return true; // Simplified for example
        
        default:
          return false;
      }
    });
  }, []);

  // Find eligible tours
  const findEligibleTours = useCallback((): Tour[] => {
    return tours.filter(tour => {
      // Skip if tour is not active
      if (!tour.isActive) return false;
      
      // Skip if already completed or skipped
      if (tourEngine.tourState.completedTours.includes(tour.id) || 
          tourEngine.tourState.skippedTours.includes(tour.id)) {
        return false;
      }
      
      // Check trigger conditions
      if (tour.triggerConditions && tour.triggerConditions.length > 0) {
        return evaluateTriggerConditions(tour.triggerConditions);
      }
      
      return true;
    }).sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority); // Higher priority first
  }, [tours, tourEngine.tourState, evaluateTriggerConditions]);

  // Auto-start eligible tours
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!autoStart || tourEngine.tourState.isPlaying) return;

    const eligible = findEligibleTours();
    if (eligible.length > 0) {
      const nextTour = eligible[0];
      
      if (debugMode) {
        console.log('Starting tour:', nextTour.name);
      }
      
      // Small delay to ensure page is fully loaded
      setTimeout(() => {
        tourEngine.startTour(nextTour);
      }, 500);
    }
  }, [findEligibleTours, autoStart, tourEngine, debugMode]);

  // Manual tour starter
  const startTourById = useCallback((tourId: string) => {
    const tour = tours.find(t => t.id === tourId);
    if (tour) {
      tourEngine.startTour(tour);
    }
  }, [tours, tourEngine]);

  // Reset tour state (useful for testing)
  const resetTourState = useCallback(() => {
    localStorage.removeItem('tour-completed');
    localStorage.removeItem('tour-skipped');
    window.location.reload();
  }, []);

  return {
    ...tourEngine,
    availableTours: findEligibleTours(),
    startTourById,
    resetTourState,
  };
};

Integration with Your App​

Here's how to integrate the tour system into your main application:

// App.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { TourProvider } from './contexts/TourContext';
import { TourOverlay } from './components/TourOverlay/TourOverlay';
import { useTourManager } from './hooks/useTourManager';
import { appTours } from './data/tours';
import './styles/tour.css';

const TourWrapper: React.FC<{ children: React.ReactNode }> = ({ children }) => {
  const tourManager = useTourManager({
    tours: appTours,
    autoStart: true,
    debugMode: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development',
  });

  const currentStep = tourManager.getCurrentStep();

  return (
    <>
      {children}
      
      {/* Render tour overlay when active */}
      {tourManager.tourState.isPlaying && currentStep && (
        <TourOverlay
          step={currentStep}
          onNext={tourManager.nextStep}
          onPrevious={tourManager.previousStep}
          onSkip={tourManager.skipTour}
          onComplete={tourManager.completeTour}
          currentStepIndex={tourManager.tourState.currentStepIndex}
          totalSteps={tourManager.tourState.currentTour?.steps.length || 0}
          isFirstStep={tourManager.tourState.currentStepIndex === 0}
          isLastStep={
            tourManager.tourState.currentStepIndex === 
            (tourManager.tourState.currentTour?.steps.length || 0) - 1
          }
        />
      )}
      
      {/* Debug panel for development */}
      {process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && (
        <TourDebugPanel tourManager={tourManager} />
      )}
    </>
  );
};

const App: React.FC = () => {
  return (
    <TourWrapper>
      <YourAppContent />
    </TourWrapper>
  );
};

export default App;

Open Source Solutions​

While building a custom tour system gives you complete control, there are excellent open source libraries that can accelerate development. Here are the most popular and well-maintained options:

1. Intro.js - The Classic Choice​

Intro.js is one of the most popular and mature tour libraries with excellent browser support.

npm install intro.js
npm install @types/intro.js  # For TypeScript support

Basic Implementation:

// components/IntroJsTour.tsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { introJs } from 'intro.js';
import 'intro.js/introjs.css';
import 'intro.js/themes/introjs-modern.css'; // Optional theme

interface IntroTourProps {
  steps: Array<{
    element: string;
    title: string;
    intro: string;
    position?: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right';
  }>;
  onComplete?: () => void;
  onExit?: () => void;
  autoStart?: boolean;
}

export const IntroJsTour: React.FC<IntroTourProps> = ({
  steps,
  onComplete,
  onExit,
  autoStart = true,
}) => {
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!autoStart) return;

    // Add data attributes to elements
    steps.forEach((step, index) => {
      const element = document.querySelector(step.element);
      if (element) {
        element.setAttribute('data-intro', step.intro);
        element.setAttribute('data-step', (index + 1).toString());
        element.setAttribute('data-title', step.title);
        if (step.position) {
          element.setAttribute('data-position', step.position);
        }
      }
    });

    // Configure and start tour
    const intro = introJs();
    
    intro.setOptions({
      nextLabel: 'Next →',
      prevLabel: '← Previous',
      skipLabel: 'Skip Tour',
      doneLabel: 'Finish',
      showProgress: true,
      showBullets: false,
      exitOnOverlayClick: false,
      keyboardNavigation: true,
      disableInteraction: false,
    });

    intro.oncomplete(() => {
      onComplete?.();
    });

    intro.onexit(() => {
      onExit?.();
    });

    intro.start();

    return () => {
      intro.exit();
    };
  }, [steps, onComplete, onExit, autoStart]);

  return null; // This component doesn't render anything
};

// utils/tourConfig.ts
import { introJs } from 'intro.js';

export const createAdvancedTour = (config: {
  steps: any[];
  onProgress?: (stepIndex: number) => void;
  onBeforeChange?: (targetElement: Element) => void;
}) => {
  const intro = introJs();

  intro.setOptions({
    nextLabel: 'Next →',
    prevLabel: '← Previous',
    skipLabel: 'Skip Tour',
    doneLabel: 'Got it!',
    showProgress: true,
    progressBarAdditionalClass: 'custom-progress',
    highlightClass: 'custom-highlight',
    showBullets: false,
    exitOnOverlayClick: false,
    keyboardNavigation: true,
    disableInteraction: false,
    scrollToElement: true,
    scrollPadding: 30,
    overlayOpacity: 0.7,
    tooltipClass: 'custom-tooltip',
  });

  // Progress tracking
  intro.onbeforechange((targetElement) => {
    config.onBeforeChange?.(targetElement);
    
    // Add custom animations
    targetElement.classList.add('tour-highlight-pulse');
    setTimeout(() => {
      targetElement.classList.remove('tour-highlight-pulse');
    }, 1000);
  });

  intro.onchange((targetElement) => {
    const currentStep = intro._currentStep;
    config.onProgress?.(currentStep);
    
    // Track analytics
    if (typeof gtag !== 'undefined') {
      gtag('event', 'tour_step_view', {
        step_number: currentStep + 1,
        step_element: targetElement.getAttribute('data-testid') || 'unknown',
      });
    }
  });

  return intro;
};

2. Reactour - React-First Approach​

Reactour is specifically designed for React applications with hooks and modern patterns.

npm install @reactour/tour
npm install @reactour/mask
npm install @reactour/popover

Implementation:

// components/ReactourTour.tsx
import React from 'react';
import { TourProvider, useTour } from '@reactour/tour';
import { Mask } from '@reactour/mask';
import { Popover, PopoverContent } from '@reactour/popover';

const TourContent: React.FC<{
  currentStep: number;
  steps: any[];
  setCurrentStep: (step: number) => void;
  setIsOpen: (isOpen: boolean) => void;
}> = ({ currentStep, steps, setCurrentStep, setIsOpen }) => {
  const isLastStep = currentStep === steps.length - 1;
  const isFirstStep = currentStep === 0;

  return (
    <PopoverContent>
      <div className="tour-content">
        <div className="tour-header">
          <h3>{steps[currentStep]?.title}</h3>
          <span className="tour-progress">
            {currentStep + 1} of {steps.length}
          </span>
        </div>
        
        <div className="tour-body">
          {steps[currentStep]?.content}
        </div>
        
        <div className="tour-actions">
          <button 
            onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
            className="tour-btn tour-btn--secondary"
          >
            Skip
          </button>
          
          <div className="tour-navigation">
            {!isFirstStep && (
              <button
                onClick={() => setCurrentStep(currentStep - 1)}
                className="tour-btn tour-btn--secondary"
              >
                Previous
              </button>
            )}
            
            <button
              onClick={() => {
                if (isLastStep) {
                  setIsOpen(false);
                } else {
                  setCurrentStep(currentStep + 1);
                }
              }}
              className="tour-btn tour-btn--primary"
            >
              {isLastStep ? 'Finish' : 'Next'}
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </PopoverContent>
  );
};

export const ReactourTourProvider: React.FC<{
  children: React.ReactNode;
  steps: Array<{
    selector: string;
    title: string;
    content: React.ReactNode;
    position?: [number, number];
    action?: (elem: Element) => void;
  }>;
}> = ({ children, steps }) => {
  return (
    <TourProvider
      steps={steps}
      components={{
        Mask: Mask,
        Popover: ({ children, ...props }) => (
          <Popover {...props}>
            {children}
          </Popover>
        ),
        Content: TourContent,
      }}
      styles={{
        popover: (base) => ({
          ...base,
          '--reactour-accent': '#3b82f6',
          borderRadius: 12,
          backgroundColor: 'white',
          boxShadow: '0 20px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)',
        }),
        mask: (base) => ({
          ...base,
          color: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)',
        }),
      }}
      onClickMask={({ setIsOpen }) => setIsOpen(false)}
      showCloseButton={false}
      showNavigation={false}
      showBadge={false}
    >
      {children}
    </TourProvider>
  );
};

// Hook for controlling tour
export const useTourControl = () => {
  const { setIsOpen, currentStep, setCurrentStep, isOpen } = useTour();
  
  const startTour = () => {
    setCurrentStep(0);
    setIsOpen(true);
  };
  
  const endTour = () => {
    setIsOpen(false);
  };
  
  return {
    startTour,
    endTour,
    isActive: isOpen,
    currentStep,
  };
};

// Usage

    {
