3. Shepherd.js - Framework Agnostic​

Shepherd.js works with any framework and provides excellent customization options.

npm install shepherd.js

Implementation:

// utils/shepherdTour.ts
import Shepherd from 'shepherd.js';
import 'shepherd.js/dist/css/shepherd.css';

export class ShepherdTourManager {
  private tour: Shepherd.Tour;
  private onComplete?: () => void;

  constructor(onComplete?: () => void) {
    this.onComplete = onComplete;
    this.tour = new Shepherd.Tour({
      useModalOverlay: true,
      defaultStepOptions: {
        classes: 'shepherd-theme-custom',
        scrollTo: true,
        cancelIcon: {
          enabled: true,
        },
        when: {
          show: this.onStepShow.bind(this),
          hide: this.onStepHide.bind(this),
        },
      },
    });

    this.tour.on('complete', () => {
      this.onComplete?.();
    });
  }

  private onStepShow() {
    // Add custom behavior when step shows
    const currentStep = this.tour.getCurrentStep();
    if (currentStep) {
      // Track analytics
      this.trackStepView(currentStep.id || 'unknown');
    }
  }

  private onStepHide() {
    // Cleanup when step hides
  }

  private trackStepView(stepId: string) {
    if (typeof gtag !== 'undefined') {
      gtag('event', 'tour_step_view', {
        step_id: stepId,
        tour_name: 'dashboard_features',
      });
    }
  }

  addStep(step: {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    text: string;
    attachTo: {
      element: string;
      on: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right';
    };
    buttons?: Array<{
      text: string;
      action: () => void;
      classes?: string;
    }>;
    beforeShowPromise?: () => Promise<void>;
  }) {
    this.tour.addStep({
      id: step.id,
      title: step.title,
      text: step.text,
      attachTo: step.attachTo,
      buttons: step.buttons || [
        {
          text: 'Skip',
          classes: 'shepherd-button-secondary',
          action: () => this.tour.complete(),
        },
        {
          text: 'Next',
          classes: 'shepherd-button-primary',
          action: () => this.tour.next(),
        },
      ],
      beforeShowPromise: step.beforeShowPromise,
    });
  }

  start() {
    this.tour.start();
  }

  complete() {
    this.tour.complete();
  }
}

// React Hook wrapper
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

export const useShepherdTour = (steps: any[], autoStart = false) => {
  const tourRef = useRef<ShepherdTourManager | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    tourRef.current = new ShepherdTourManager(() => {
      localStorage.setItem('tour-completed', 'true');
    });

    // Add all steps
    steps.forEach(step => {
      tourRef.current!.addStep(step);
    });

    if (autoStart && !localStorage.getItem('tour-completed')) {
      tourRef.current.start();
    }

    return () => {
      if (tourRef.current) {
        tourRef.current.complete();
      }
    };
  }, [steps, autoStart]);

  const startTour = () => {
    tourRef.current?.start();
  };

  const completeTour = () => {
    tourRef.current?.complete();
  };

  return { startTour, completeTour };
};

// Usage in React component
const DashboardWithShepherd = () => {
  const tourSteps = [
    {
      id: 'welcome',
      title: 'Welcome to the New Dashboard! 🎉',
      text: `
        <p>We've added some exciting new features. Let's take a quick tour!</p>
        <div class="tour-features">
          <span class="feature-badge">📊 Enhanced Analytics</span>
          <span class="feature-badge">⚡ Quick Actions</span>
          <span class="feature-badge">🔔 Smart Notifications</span>
        </div>
      `,
      attachTo: {
        element: 'body',
        on: 'top' as const,
      },
    },
    {
      id: 'analytics',
      title: 'Enhanced Analytics Widget',
      text: `
        <p>Your analytics now include:</p>
        <ul>
          <li>📊 Real-time data updates</li>
          <li>🎯 Custom date range selection</li>
          <li>📈 Advanced filtering options</li>
        </ul>
        <p>Click any chart to drill down into detailed metrics.</p>
      `,
      attachTo: {
        element: '[data-testid="analytics-widget"]',
        on: 'bottom' as const,
      },
      beforeShowPromise: () => {
        return new Promise(resolve => {
          // Ensure element is visible before showing step
          const element = document.querySelector('[data-testid="analytics-widget"]');
          if (element) {
            element.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center' });
            setTimeout(resolve, 500);
          } else {
            resolve();
          }
        });
      },
    },
  ];

  const { startTour } = useShepherdTour(tourSteps, true);

  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={startTour} className="start-tour-btn">
        Take a Tour
      </button>
      {/* Your dashboard content */}
    </div>
  );
};

4. Driver.js - Lightweight and Modern​

Driver.js is a lightweight, modern library with great performance.

npm install driver.js

Implementation:

// utils/driverTour.ts
import { driver, DriveStep } from 'driver.js';
import 'driver.js/dist/driver.css';

export class DriverTourManager {
  private driverObj: any;

  constructor(config?: {
    onHighlightStarted?: (element: Element, step: DriveStep) => void;
    onHighlighted?: (element: Element, step: DriveStep) => void;
    onDeselected?: (element: Element, step: DriveStep) => void;
    onDestroyed?: () => void;
  }) {
    this.driverObj = driver({
      showProgress: true,
      showButtons: ['next', 'previous', 'close'],
      steps: [], // Will be populated later
      onHighlightStarted: config?.onHighlightStarted,
      onHighlighted: config?.onHighlighted,
      onDeselected: config?.onDeselected,
      onDestroyed: config?.onDestroyed,
    });
  }

  setSteps(steps: DriveStep[]) {
    this.driverObj.setSteps(steps);
  }

  start() {
    this.driverObj.drive();
  }

  destroy() {
    this.driverObj.destroy();
  }

  highlight(element: string) {
    this.driverObj.highlight({
      element,
      popover: {
        title: 'Highlighted Feature',
        description: 'This is an important feature to note.',
      },
    });
  }
}

// React Hook
export const useDriverTour = () => {
  const [tourManager] = useState(() => new DriverTourManager({
    onDestroyed: () => {
      localStorage.setItem('driver-tour-completed', 'true');
    },
    onHighlighted: (element, step) => {
      // Add pulse animation
      element.classList.add('driver-highlighted');
      
      // Track step view
      if (typeof gtag !== 'undefined') {
        gtag('event', 'tour_step_view', {
          step_index: step.element,
          tour_type: 'driver_js',
        });
      }
    },
    onDeselected: (element) => {
      element.classList.remove('driver-highlighted');
    },
  }));

  const startTour = (steps: DriveStep[]) => {
    tourManager.setSteps(steps);
    tourManager.start();
  };

  const highlightElement = (element: string) => {
    tourManager.highlight(element);
  };

  return { startTour, highlightElement, destroy: () => tourManager.destroy() };
};

// Component usage
const FeatureTour = () => {
  const { startTour } = useDriverTour();

  const tourSteps: DriveStep[] = [
    {
      element: 'body',
      popover: {
        title: 'Welcome to the Enhanced Dashboard! 🚀',
        description: `
          <div class="tour-welcome">
            <p>Discover our latest features that will boost your productivity:</p>
            <div class="feature-grid">
              <div class="feature-item">
                <span class="feature-icon">📊</span>
                <span>Real-time Analytics</span>
              </div>
              <div class="feature-item">
                <span class="feature-icon">⚡</span>
                <span>Quick Actions</span>
              </div>
              <div class="feature-item">
                <span class="feature-icon">🔔</span>
                <span>Smart Notifications</span>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        `,
        side: 'bottom',
        align: 'center',
      },
    },
    {
      element: '[data-testid="analytics-widget"]',
      popover: {
        title: '📊 Enhanced Analytics',
        description: `
          <p>Your analytics dashboard now features:</p>
          <ul class="feature-list">
            <li>✨ Real-time data streaming</li>
            <li>🎯 Advanced filtering and segmentation</li>
            <li>📈 Predictive trend analysis</li>
            <li>📊 Custom dashboard creation</li>
          </ul>
          <div class="tour-tip">
            💡 <strong>Pro tip:</strong> Click any chart to drill down into detailed metrics!
          </div>
        `,
        side: 'bottom',
        align: 'start',
      },
    },
    {
      element: '[data-testid="quick-actions"]',
      popover: {
        title: '⚡ Quick Actions Toolbar',
        description: `
          <p>Save time with instant access to common tasks:</p>
          <div class="action-showcase">
            <div class="action-item">
              <span class="action-icon">➕</span>
              <span>Create new items</span>
            </div>
            <div class="action-item">
              <span class="action-icon">🔍</span>
              <span>Smart search & filter</span>
            </div>
            <div class="action-item">
              <span class="action-icon">🔄</span>
              <span>Bulk operations</span>
            </div>
          </div>
        `,
        side: 'bottom',
        align: 'center',
      },
    },
  ];

  useEffect(() => {
    // Auto-start tour for new users
    const hasSeenTour = localStorage.getItem('driver-tour-completed');
    if (!hasSeenTour) {
      setTimeout(() => startTour(tourSteps), 1000);
    }
  }, []);

  return (
    <button 
      onClick={() => startTour(tourSteps)}
      className="tour-trigger-btn"
    >
      🎯 Take Feature Tour
    </button>
  );
};

Library Comparison and Recommendations​

LibraryBundle SizeReact IntegrationCustomizationTypeScriptBest For
Intro.js~20KBGoodHighPartialTraditional web apps, maximum browser support
Reactour~15KBExcellentHighExcellentReact-first projects, modern styling
Shepherd.js~25KBGoodVery HighGoodComplex tours, framework agnostic
Driver.js~12KBGoodMediumGoodLightweight tours, performance-critical apps

Choosing the Right Library​

Use Intro.js when:

  • You need maximum browser compatibility
  • Working with legacy codebases
  • Want extensive documentation and community support
  • Need proven stability in production

Use Reactour when:

  • Building React applications
  • Want modern hooks-based API
  • Need excellent TypeScript support
  • Prefer component-based architecture

Use Shepherd.js when:

  • Need maximum customization flexibility
  • Building complex, multi-step workflows
  • Working with multiple frameworks
  • Want advanced tour features (branching, conditionals)

Use Driver.js when:

  • Bundle size is critical
  • Need simple, straightforward tours
  • Want modern, clean API
  • Performance is a priority

Hybrid Approach: Combining Libraries​

You can also combine libraries for different use cases:

// tourStrategy.ts
import { TourLibrary, TourStep } from './types';

export class TourStrategy {
  private getOptimalLibrary(steps: TourStep[], context: any): TourLibrary {
    // Use lightweight library for simple tours
    if (steps.length <= 3 && !context.needsCustomization) {
      return 'driver';
    }
    
    // Use React-specific library for component-heavy tours
    if (context.isReactApp && steps.some(s => s.hasReactContent)) {
      return 'reactour';
    }
    
    // Use Shepherd for complex business workflows
    if (steps.length > 8 || context.needsBranching) {
      return 'shepherd';
    }
    
    // Default to Intro.js for compatibility
    return 'introjs';
  }

  async createTour(steps: TourStep[], context: any) {
    const library = this.getOptimalLibrary(steps, context);
    
    switch (library) {
      case 'driver':
        const { DriverTourManager } = await import('./drivers/driverTour');
        return new DriverTourManager();
      
      case 'reactour':
        const { ReactourManager } = await import('./drivers/reactourTour');
        return new ReactourManager();
      
      case 'shepherd':
        const { ShepherdTourManager } = await import('./drivers/shepherdTour');
        return new ShepherdTourManager();
      
      default:
        const { IntroJsManager } = await import('./drivers/introJsTour');
        return new IntroJsManager();
    }
  }
}

Quick Start Templates​

Here are ready-to-use templates for each library:

Intro.js Quick Start:

# Install
npm install intro.js @types/intro.js

# Add to your component
import { introJs } from 'intro.js';
import 'intro.js/introjs.css';

// Initialize tour
const startTour = () => {
  introJs().setOptions({
    steps: [
      {
        element: '#step1',
        intro: 'This is your first feature!',
        title: 'Welcome'
      }
    ]
  }).start();
};

Reactour Quick Start:

# Install
npm install @reactour/tour @reactour/mask @reactour/popover

# Wrap your app
import { TourProvider } from '@reactour/tour';

const steps = [
  { selector: '#step1', content: 'Welcome to our app!' }
];

<TourProvider steps={steps}>
  <App />
</TourProvider>

Shepherd.js Quick Start:

# Install
npm install shepherd.js

# Create tour
import Shepherd from 'shepherd.js';

const tour = new Shepherd.Tour({
  defaultStepOptions: { scrollTo: true }
});

tour.addStep({
  title: 'Welcome!',
  text: 'This is your first step',
  attachTo: { element: '#step1', on: 'bottom' }
});

tour.start();

Driver.js Quick Start:

# Install
npm install driver.js

# Create tour
import { driver } from 'driver.js';

const driverObj = driver({
  steps: [
    { element: '#step1', popover: { title: 'Title', description: 'Description' } }
  ]
});

driverObj.drive();

Advanced Features​

Analytics Integration​

Track tour performance and user engagement:

// utils/tourAnalytics.ts
interface TourAnalyticsEvent {
  tourId: string;
  stepId: string;
  action: 'start' | 'next' | 'previous' | 'skip' | 'complete';
  timestamp: number;
  userSegment?: string;
}

export class TourAnalytics {
  private events: TourAnalyticsEvent[] = [];

  trackEvent(event: Omit<TourAnalyticsEvent, 'timestamp'>) {
    const fullEvent: TourAnalyticsEvent = {
      ...event,
      timestamp: Date.now(),
    };
    
    this.events.push(fullEvent);
    
    // Send to your analytics service
    this.sendToAnalytics(fullEvent);
  }

  private sendToAnalytics(event: TourAnalyticsEvent) {
    // Integration with your analytics platform
    if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && (window as any).gtag) {
      (window as any).gtag('event', 'tour_interaction', {
        tour_id: event.tourId,
        step_id: event.stepId,
        action: event.action,
        user_segment: event.userSegment,
      });
    }
    
    // Or send to your custom analytics endpoint
    fetch('/api/analytics/tour-events', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify(event),
    }).catch(console.error);
  }

  getTourMetrics(tourId: string) {
    const tourEvents = this.events.filter(e => e.tourId === tourId);
    const startEvents = tourEvents.filter(e => e.action === 'start');
    const completeEvents = tourEvents.filter(e => e.action === 'complete');
    const skipEvents = tourEvents.filter(e => e.action === 'skip');
    
    return {
      starts: startEvents.length,
      completions: completeEvents.length,
      skips: skipEvents.length,
      completionRate: startEvents.length > 0 ? completeEvents.length / startEvents.length : 0,
      skipRate: startEvents.length > 0 ? skipEvents.length / startEvents.length : 0,
    };
  }
}

A/B Testing Support​

Test different tour variations:

// utils/tourVariants.ts
interface TourVariant {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  tour: Tour;
  weight: number; // Percentage allocation
}

export class TourVariantManager {
  private variants: Map<string, TourVariant[]> = new Map();

  addVariant(baseTrackId: string, variant: TourVariant) {
    if (!this.variants.has(baseTrackId)) {
      this.variants.set(baseTrackId, []);
    }
    this.variants.get(baseTrackId)!.push(variant);
  }

  getVariantForUser(baseTrackId: string, userId: string): Tour | null {
    const variants = this.variants.get(baseTrackId);
    if (!variants || variants.length === 0) return null;

    // Use consistent hash of user ID for stable variant assignment
    const hash = this.hashString(userId + baseTrackId);
    const totalWeight = variants.reduce((sum, v) => sum + v.weight, 0);
    const target = (hash % 100) / 100 * totalWeight;
    
    let cumulative = 0;
    for (const variant of variants) {
      cumulative += variant.weight;
      if (target <= cumulative) {
        return variant.tour;
      }
    }
    
    return variants[0].tour; // Fallback
  }

  private hashString(str: string): number {
    let hash = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
      const char = str.charCodeAt(i);
      hash = ((hash << 5) - hash) + char;
      hash = hash & hash; // Convert to 32-bit integer
    }
    return Math.abs(hash);
  }
}

Best Practices and Tips​

🎯 Content Guidelines​

  1. Keep it concise: Limit steps to 5-7 for optimal engagement
  2. Use progressive disclosure: Start with overview, then dive into specifics
  3. Include visuals: Use emojis and bullet points for better readability
  4. Provide context: Explain the "why" behind features, not just the "how"

🔧 Technical Considerations​

  1. Performance: Use lazy loading for tour components
  2. Accessibility: Ensure keyboard navigation and screen reader compatibility
  3. Mobile responsiveness: Test tours on different screen sizes
  4. Error handling: Gracefully handle missing target elements

📊 Measurement and Optimization​

  1. Track completion rates: Monitor which steps cause dropoffs
  2. Gather feedback: Add optional feedback collection at tour end
  3. A/B testing: Test different content and flows
  4. Timing: Experiment with when tours are triggered

🎨 Design Principles​

  1. Non-intrusive: Allow users to continue working while touring
  2. Contextual: Show tours when users encounter relevant features
  3. Skippable: Always provide an easy exit option
  4. Memorable: Use consistent styling that matches your brand

Conclusion​

Interactive tour guides are powerful tools for improving user onboarding and feature adoption. By implementing a flexible, well-designed tour system, you can:

  • Reduce time to value for new users
  • Increase feature adoption for existing users
  • Decrease support burden through proactive guidance
  • Improve user satisfaction with contextual help

The tour system we've built provides a solid foundation that can be extended with additional features like:

  • Multi-step forms guidance
  • Video integration
  • Branching tour paths
  • Personalized content based on user behavior
  • Integration with help desk systems

Remember to continuously gather user feedback and iterate on your tour content and timing. The best tours feel helpful rather than intrusive, and they evolve based on real user needs and behaviors.

Start with simple tours for your most important features, measure their effectiveness, and gradually expand your tour system as you learn what works best for your users and application.

Want to learn more about user experience optimization? This guide provides a solid foundation for building interactive user experiences that enhance feature discovery and adoption.

item.title: Handling Rate Limiting in NestJS for Production Microservices
item.description: Rate limiting is a critical security and performance mechanism in production microservice architectures. It protects your services from abuse, ensures fair resource allocation, and maintains system stability under high load. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore how to implement robust, scalable rate limiting in NestJS applications designed for microservice environments.
item.content:encoded:
Rate limiting is a critical security and performance mechanism in production microservice architectures. It protects your services from abuse, ensures fair resource allocation, and maintains system stability under high load. In this comprehensive guide, we'll explore how to implement robust, scalable rate limiting in NestJS applications designed for microservice environments.

Why Rate Limiting is Critical in Microservices​

🛡️ Security Benefits​

  • DDoS Protection: Prevents overwhelming individual services with excessive requests
  • API Abuse Prevention: Stops malicious actors from exhausting system resources
  • Brute Force Attack Mitigation: Limits login attempts and sensitive operations
  • Resource Protection: Ensures no single client can monopolize service capacity

⚡ Performance Benefits​

  • Fair Resource Allocation: Ensures all users get equitable access to services
  • Cascade Failure Prevention: Prevents one overloaded service from affecting others
  • Cost Control: Manages computational and bandwidth costs in cloud environments
  • SLA Compliance: Helps maintain service level agreements under varying loads

🏗️ Microservice-Specific Challenges​

  • Distributed State Management: Rate limits must work across multiple service instances
  • Service-to-Service Communication: Internal APIs need different limits than public ones
  • Dynamic Scaling: Rate limits must adapt to auto-scaling scenarios
  • Cross-Service Coordination: Shared limits across multiple related services

Popular Open Source Rate Limiting Libraries​

Before implementing custom rate limiting solutions, consider these battle-tested libraries that can significantly speed up development:

🚀 @nestjs/throttler​

The official NestJS throttling library provides simple, decorator-based rate limiting.

// Installation
npm install @nestjs/throttler

// Basic setup
import { ThrottlerModule, ThrottlerGuard } from '@nestjs/throttler';
import { APP_GUARD } from '@nestjs/core';

@Module({
  imports: [
    ThrottlerModule.forRoot([
      {
        name: 'short',
        ttl: 1000,  // 1 second
        limit: 3,   // 3 requests per second
      },
      {
        name: 'medium',
        ttl: 10000, // 10 seconds
        limit: 20,  // 20 requests per 10 seconds
      },
      {
        name: 'long',
        ttl: 60000, // 1 minute
        limit: 100, // 100 requests per minute
      },
    ]),
  ],
  providers: [
    {
      provide: APP_GUARD,
      useClass: ThrottlerGuard,
    },
  ],
})
export class AppModule {}

// Usage in controllers
import { Throttle } from '@nestjs/throttler';

@Controller('api')
export class ApiController {
  @Get('public')
  @Throttle({ default: { limit: 10, ttl: 60000 } })
  getPublicData() {
    return { data: 'Limited to 10 requests per minute' };
  }

  @Post('auth/login')
  @Throttle({ default: { limit: 5, ttl: 300000 } }) // 5 attempts per 5 minutes
  login(@Body() credentials: any) {
    return { token: 'jwt-token' };
  }
}

⚡ express-rate-limit​

A mature Express.js rate limiting middleware that works seamlessly with NestJS.

// Installation
npm install express-rate-limit

// Global setup
import rateLimit from 'express-rate-limit';

const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);

// Global rate limiting
app.use(
  rateLimit({
    windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, // 15 minutes
    max: 100, // Limit each IP to 100 requests per windowMs
    message: {
      error: 'Too many requests, please try again later.',
      retryAfter: '15 minutes',
    },
    standardHeaders: true, // Return rate limit info in headers
    legacyHeaders: false,
    // Redis store for distributed rate limiting
    store: new RedisStore({
      sendCommand: (...args: string[]) => redisClient.call(...args),
    }),
  })
);

// Route-specific limiting
import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express';

const loginLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, // 15 minutes
  max: 5, // Limit each IP to 5 login requests per windowMs
  message: 'Too many login attempts, please try again later.',
  skipSuccessfulRequests: true, // Don't count successful requests
});

@Controller('auth')
export class AuthController {
  @Post('login')
  @UseInterceptors(
    // Apply rate limiting middleware as interceptor
    (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => 
      loginLimiter(req, res, next)
  )
  login(@Body() credentials: any) {
    return { token: 'jwt-token' };
  }
}

🔄 bottleneck​

Advanced rate limiting with queuing, clustering, and Redis support.

// Installation
npm install bottleneck

// Service implementation
import Bottleneck from 'bottleneck';
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';

@Injectable()
export class AdvancedRateLimitService {
  private limiters = new Map<string, Bottleneck>();

  constructor() {
    // Create different limiters for different use cases
    this.setupLimiters();
  }

  private setupLimiters() {
    // API rate limiter with Redis clustering
    this.limiters.set('api', new Bottleneck({
      reservoir: 100,           // Initial capacity
      reservoirRefreshAmount: 100, // Tokens to add
      reservoirRefreshInterval: 60 * 1000, // Every minute
      maxConcurrent: 10,        // Max concurrent requests
      minTime: 100,             // Min time between requests (100ms)
      
      // Redis clustering for distributed rate limiting
      datastore: 'redis',
      clearDatastore: false,
      clientOptions: {
        host: 'localhost',
        port: 6379,
      },
      clusterNodes: [
        { host: 'redis-1', port: 6379 },
        { host: 'redis-2', port: 6379 },
      ],
    }));

    // Premium API with higher limits
    this.limiters.set('premium', new Bottleneck({
      reservoir: 1000,
      reservoirRefreshAmount: 1000,
      reservoirRefreshInterval: 60 * 1000,
      maxConcurrent: 50,
      minTime: 20,
    }));

    // Heavy processing limiter
    this.limiters.set('processing', new Bottleneck({
      maxConcurrent: 3,         // Only 3 heavy operations at once
      minTime: 2000,            // 2 seconds between operations
    }));
  }

  async executeWithRateLimit<T>(
    limiterType: string,
    operation: () => Promise<T>,
    priority?: number
  ): Promise<T> {
    const limiter = this.limiters.get(limiterType);
    if (!limiter) {
      throw new Error(`Unknown limiter type: ${limiterType}`);
    }

    return limiter.schedule({ priority }, operation);
  }

  async checkRateLimit(
    limiterType: string,
    weight: number = 1
  ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; msBeforeNext: number }> {
    const limiter = this.limiters.get(limiterType);
    if (!limiter) {
      return { allowed: false, msBeforeNext: 0 };
    }

    try {
      const result = await limiter.check(weight);
      return {
        allowed: result >= 0,
        msBeforeNext: result < 0 ? Math.abs(result) : 0,
      };
    } catch (error) {
      return { allowed: false, msBeforeNext: 1000 };
    }
  }

  // Get limiter statistics
  getStats(limiterType: string) {
    const limiter = this.limiters.get(limiterType);
    if (!limiter) return null;

    return {
      running: limiter.running(),
      queued: limiter.queued(),
      reservoir: limiter.reservoir(),
      capacity: limiter.capacity,
    };
  }
}

// Usage in controllers
@Controller('api')
export class ApiController {
  constructor(
    private readonly rateLimitService: AdvancedRateLimitService
  ) {}

  @Get('data')
  async getData() {
    return this.rateLimitService.executeWithRateLimit(
      'api',
      async () => {
        // Your API logic here
        return { data: 'API response' };
      }
    );
  }

  @Post('heavy-process')
  async heavyProcess(@Body() data: any) {
    const check = await this.rateLimitService.checkRateLimit('processing');
    
    if (!check.allowed) {
      throw new HttpException(
        {
          message: 'Processing queue full',
          retryAfter: Math.ceil(check.msBeforeNext / 1000),
        },
        HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
      );
    }

    return this.rateLimitService.executeWithRateLimit(
      'processing',
      async () => {
        // Heavy processing logic
        await this.performHeavyOperation(data);
        return { status: 'completed' };
      },
      5 // High priority
    );
  }

  @Get('stats')
  getSystemStats() {
    return {
      api: this.rateLimitService.getStats('api'),
      premium: this.rateLimitService.getStats('premium'),
      processing: this.rateLimitService.getStats('processing'),
    };
  }
}

🏪 ioredis-rate-limiter​

Redis-based rate limiting with sliding window implementation.

// Installation
npm install ioredis-rate-limiter ioredis

// Service implementation
import RateLimiter from 'ioredis-rate-limiter';
import Redis from 'ioredis';
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';

@Injectable()
export class RedisRateLimitService {
  private redis: Redis;
  private limiters = new Map<string, RateLimiter>();

  constructor() {
    this.redis = new Redis({
      host: 'localhost',
      port: 6379,
      retryDelayOnFailover: 100,
    });

    this.setupLimiters();
  }

  private setupLimiters() {
    // API rate limiter - 100 requests per minute
    this.limiters.set('api', new RateLimiter({
      redis: this.redis,
      key: (id: string) => `rate_limit:api:${id}`,
      window: 60000,        // 1 minute window
      limit: 100,           // 100 requests per window
    }));

    // Login rate limiter - 5 attempts per 15 minutes
    this.limiters.set('login', new RateLimiter({
      redis: this.redis,
      key: (id: string) => `rate_limit:login:${id}`,
      window: 15 * 60000,   // 15 minutes
      limit: 5,             // 5 attempts
    }));

    // Premium API - 1000 requests per minute
    this.limiters.set('premium', new RateLimiter({
      redis: this.redis,
      key: (id: string) => `rate_limit:premium:${id}`,
      window: 60000,
      limit: 1000,
    }));
  }

  async checkLimit(
    type: string,
    identifier: string,
    cost: number = 1
  ): Promise<{
    allowed: boolean;
    remaining: number;
    resetTime: Date;
    totalHits: number;
  }> {
    const limiter = this.limiters.get(type);
    if (!limiter) {
      throw new Error(`Unknown rate limiter type: ${type}`);
    }

    try {
      const result = await limiter.check(identifier, cost);
      
      return {
        allowed: result.allowed,
        remaining: result.remaining,
        resetTime: new Date(result.resetTime),
        totalHits: result.totalHits,
      };
    } catch (error) {
      // Fallback in case of Redis issues
      console.error('Rate limit check failed:', error);
      return {
        allowed: true, // Fail open for availability
        remaining: 0,
        resetTime: new Date(Date.now() + 60000),
        totalHits: 0,
      };
    }
  }

  async getRemainingQuota(type: string, identifier: string): Promise<number> {
    const result = await this.checkLimit(type, identifier, 0); // Cost 0 for check only
    return result.remaining;
  }
}

// Guard implementation
@Injectable()
export class RedisRateLimitGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(
    private readonly rateLimitService: RedisRateLimitService,
    private readonly reflector: Reflector
  ) {}

  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest();
    const response = context.switchToHttp().getResponse();
    
    // Get rate limit configuration from decorator
    const config = this.reflector.get<{
      type: string;
      identifier?: (req: any) => string;
      cost?: number;
    }>('REDIS_RATE_LIMIT', context.getHandler());

    if (!config) {
      return true; // No rate limiting configured
    }

    // Generate identifier
    const identifier = config.identifier 
      ? config.identifier(request)
      : request.ip;

    // Check rate limit
    const result = await this.rateLimitService.checkLimit(
      config.type,
      identifier,
      config.cost || 1
    );

    // Set headers
    response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining);
    response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime.toISOString());
    response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Total', result.totalHits);

    if (!result.allowed) {
      response.setHeader('Retry-After', Math.ceil((result.resetTime.getTime() - Date.now()) / 1000));
      
      throw new HttpException(
        {
          statusCode: HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
          message: 'Rate limit exceeded',
          retryAfter: result.resetTime.toISOString(),
        },
        HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
      );
    }

    return true;
  }
}

// Decorator for easy usage
export const RedisRateLimit = (config: {
  type: string;
  identifier?: (req: any) => string;
  cost?: number;
}) => SetMetadata('REDIS_RATE_LIMIT', config);

// Usage example
@Controller('api')
@UseGuards(RedisRateLimitGuard)
export class ApiController {
  @Get('data')
  @RedisRateLimit({
    type: 'api',
    identifier: (req) => req.ip,
  })
  getData() {
    return { data: 'API response' };
  }

  @Post('login')
  @RedisRateLimit({
    type: 'login',
    identifier: (req) => `${req.ip}:${req.body.email}`,
  })
  login(@Body() credentials: any) {
    return { token: 'jwt-token' };
  }

  @Get('premium')
  @RedisRateLimit({
    type: 'premium',
    identifier: (req) => req.user?.id || req.ip,
    cost: 5, // This endpoint costs 5 "points"
  })
  getPremiumData() {
    return { data: 'Premium API response' };
  }
}

Rate Limiting Strategies for Microservices​

1. Token Bucket Algorithm​

The token bucket algorithm is ideal for allowing bursts while maintaining average rate limits.

// rate-limiting/token-bucket.service.ts
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis';

interface TokenBucketConfig {
  capacity: number;      // Maximum tokens in bucket
  refillRate: number;    // Tokens added per second
  windowSize: number;    // Time window in seconds
}

@Injectable()
export class TokenBucketService {
  constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) {}

  async checkRateLimit(
    key: string,
    config: TokenBucketConfig,
    tokensRequested: number = 1
  ): Promise<{
    allowed: boolean;
    remainingTokens: number;
    resetTime: number;
    retryAfter?: number;
  }> {
    const script = `
      local key = KEYS[1]
      local capacity = tonumber(ARGV[1])
      local refillRate = tonumber(ARGV[2])
      local windowSize = tonumber(ARGV[3])
      local tokensRequested = tonumber(ARGV[4])
      local now = tonumber(ARGV[5])
      
      -- Get current bucket state
      local bucket = redis.call('HMGET', key, 'tokens', 'lastRefill')
      local tokens = tonumber(bucket[1]) or capacity
      local lastRefill = tonumber(bucket[2]) or now
      
      -- Calculate tokens to add based on time elapsed
      local elapsed = math.max(0, now - lastRefill)
      local tokensToAdd = math.floor(elapsed * refillRate)
      tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + tokensToAdd)
      
      -- Check if request can be fulfilled
      local allowed = tokens >= tokensRequested
      local remainingTokens = tokens
      local retryAfter = 0
      
      if allowed then
        remainingTokens = tokens - tokensRequested
        -- Update bucket state
        redis.call('HMSET', key, 'tokens', remainingTokens, 'lastRefill', now)
        redis.call('EXPIRE', key, windowSize * 2)
      else
        -- Calculate retry after time
        local tokensNeeded = tokensRequested - tokens
        retryAfter = math.ceil(tokensNeeded / refillRate)
      end
      
      return {
        allowed and 1 or 0,
        remainingTokens,
        now + (capacity - remainingTokens) / refillRate,
        retryAfter
      }
    `;

    const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
    const result = await this.redis.eval(
      script,
      1,
      key,
      config.capacity,
      config.refillRate,
      config.windowSize,
      tokensRequested,
      now
    ) as [number, number, number, number];

    return {
      allowed: result[0] === 1,
      remainingTokens: result[1],
      resetTime: result[2],
      retryAfter: result[3] > 0 ? result[3] : undefined,
    };
  }
}

2. Sliding Window Algorithm​

Sliding window provides more accurate rate limiting by tracking requests in a rolling time window.

// rate-limiting/sliding-window.service.ts
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis';

interface SlidingWindowConfig {
  limit: number;         // Maximum requests per window
  windowMs: number;      // Window size in milliseconds
  precision: number;     // Sub-window precision (e.g., 10 for 10 sub-windows)
}

@Injectable()
export class SlidingWindowService {
  constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) {}

  async checkRateLimit(
    key: string,
    config: SlidingWindowConfig
  ): Promise<{
    allowed: boolean;
    remaining: number;
    resetTime: number;
    currentUsage: number;
  }> {
    const script = `
      local key = KEYS[1]
      local limit = tonumber(ARGV[1])
      local windowMs = tonumber(ARGV[2])
      local precision = tonumber(ARGV[3])
      local now = tonumber(ARGV[4])
      
      -- Calculate sub-window size
      local subWindowMs = windowMs / precision
      local currentWindow = math.floor(now / subWindowMs)
      local windowStart = currentWindow - precision + 1
      
      -- Clean old sub-windows
      redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, 0, windowStart - 1)
      
      -- Count current requests in the sliding window
      local currentCount = 0
      local subWindows = redis.call('ZRANGE', key, 0, -1, 'WITHSCORES')
      
      for i = 1, #subWindows, 2 do
        local subWindow = tonumber(subWindows[i + 1])
        local count = tonumber(subWindows[i])
        
        if subWindow >= windowStart then
          -- Calculate overlap percentage for partial windows
          local overlap = 1
          if subWindow == windowStart then
            local subWindowTime = subWindow * subWindowMs
            local windowTime = now - windowMs
            overlap = math.max(0, (subWindowTime + subWindowMs - windowTime) / subWindowMs)
          end
          currentCount = currentCount + (count * overlap)
        end
      end
      
      local allowed = currentCount < limit
      local remaining = math.max(0, limit - currentCount - 1)
      
      if allowed then
        -- Increment counter for current sub-window
        redis.call('ZINCRBY', key, 1, currentWindow)
        redis.call('EXPIRE', key, math.ceil(windowMs / 1000) * 2)
      end
      
      local resetTime = (currentWindow + 1) * subWindowMs
      
      return {
        allowed and 1 or 0,
        remaining,
        resetTime,
        currentCount + (allowed and 1 or 0)
      }
    `;

    const now = Date.now();
    const result = await this.redis.eval(
      script,
      1,
      key,
      config.limit,
      config.windowMs,
      config.precision,
      now
    ) as [number, number, number, number];

    return {
      allowed: result[0] === 1,
      remaining: result[1],
      resetTime: result[2],
      currentUsage: result[3],
    };
  }
}

Advanced Rate Limiting Guard​

Create a flexible, configurable rate limiting guard that supports multiple algorithms and strategies.

// guards/rate-limit.guard.ts
import {
  Injectable,
  CanActivate,
  ExecutionContext,
  HttpException,
  HttpStatus,
  Inject,
} from '@nestjs/common';
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core';
import { Request, Response } from 'express';
import { TokenBucketService } from '../rate-limiting/token-bucket.service';
import { SlidingWindowService } from '../rate-limiting/sliding-window.service';
import { RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS } from '../decorators/rate-limit.decorator';

export interface RateLimitOptions {
  algorithm: 'token-bucket' | 'sliding-window' | 'fixed-window';
  keyGenerator?: (req: Request) => string;
  skipIf?: (req: Request) => boolean;
  onLimitReached?: (req: Request, res: Response) => void;
  
  // Token bucket specific
  capacity?: number;
  refillRate?: number;
  
  // Sliding/Fixed window specific
  limit?: number;
  windowMs?: number;
  precision?: number; // For sliding window
  
  // Common options
  message?: string;
  standardHeaders?: boolean;
  legacyHeaders?: boolean;
  skipSuccessfulRequests?: boolean;
  skipFailedRequests?: boolean;
}

@Injectable()
export class RateLimitGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(
    private readonly reflector: Reflector,
    private readonly tokenBucket: TokenBucketService,
    private readonly slidingWindow: SlidingWindowService,
    @Inject('CONFIG_SERVICE') private readonly config: any
  ) {}

  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
    const request = context.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request>();
    const response = context.switchToHttp().getResponse<Response>();
    
    // Get rate limit options from decorator or global config
    const options = this.getRateLimitOptions(context);
    
    if (!options) {
      return true; // No rate limiting configured
    }

    // Check if request should be skipped
    if (options.skipIf && options.skipIf(request)) {
      return true;
    }

    // Generate rate limit key
    const key = this.generateKey(request, options);
    
    // Apply rate limiting based on algorithm
    const result = await this.applyRateLimit(key, options);
    
    // Set response headers
    this.setHeaders(response, result, options);
    
    if (!result.allowed) {
      // Execute custom handler if provided
      if (options.onLimitReached) {
        options.onLimitReached(request, response);
      }
      
      // Throw rate limit exceeded exception
      throw new HttpException(
        {
          statusCode: HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
          message: options.message || 'Rate limit exceeded',
          error: 'Too Many Requests',
          retryAfter: result.retryAfter,
        },
        HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
      );
    }

    return true;
  }

  private getRateLimitOptions(context: ExecutionContext): RateLimitOptions | null {
    // Check method-level decorator first
    const methodOptions = this.reflector.get<RateLimitOptions>(
      RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS,
      context.getHandler()
    );
    
    if (methodOptions) {
      return methodOptions;
    }

    // Check class-level decorator
    const classOptions = this.reflector.get<RateLimitOptions>(
      RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS,
      context.getClass()
    );
    
    if (classOptions) {
      return classOptions;
    }

    // Return global default options if configured
    return this.config.get('rateLimit.default');
  }

  private generateKey(request: Request, options: RateLimitOptions): string {
    if (options.keyGenerator) {
      return options.keyGenerator(request);
    }

    // Default key generation strategy
    const ip = request.ip || request.connection.remoteAddress;
    const userId = (request as any).user?.id || 'anonymous';
    const route = `${request.method}:${request.route?.path || request.path}`;
    
    return `rate_limit:${ip}:${userId}:${route}`;
  }

  private async applyRateLimit(
    key: string,
    options: RateLimitOptions
  ): Promise<{
    allowed: boolean;
    remaining?: number;
    resetTime?: number;
    retryAfter?: number;
    currentUsage?: number;
  }> {
    switch (options.algorithm) {
      case 'token-bucket':
        return this.tokenBucket.checkRateLimit(key, {
          capacity: options.capacity || 10,
          refillRate: options.refillRate || 1,
          windowSize: Math.floor((options.windowMs || 60000) / 1000),
        });

      case 'sliding-window':
        return this.slidingWindow.checkRateLimit(key, {
          limit: options.limit || 100,
          windowMs: options.windowMs || 60000,
          precision: options.precision || 10,
        });

      case 'fixed-window':
        return this.applyFixedWindow(key, {
          limit: options.limit || 100,
          windowMs: options.windowMs || 60000,
        });

      default:
        throw new Error(`Unknown rate limiting algorithm: ${options.algorithm}`);
    }
  }

  private async applyFixedWindow(
    key: string,
    config: { limit: number; windowMs: number }
  ): Promise<any> {
    // Simple fixed window implementation using Redis
    const window = Math.floor(Date.now() / config.windowMs);
    const windowKey = `${key}:${window}`;
    
    const current = await this.tokenBucket['redis'].incr(windowKey);
    await this.tokenBucket['redis'].expire(windowKey, Math.ceil(config.windowMs / 1000));
    
    const allowed = current <= config.limit;
    const remaining = Math.max(0, config.limit - current);
    const resetTime = (window + 1) * config.windowMs;
    
    return {
      allowed,
      remaining,
      resetTime,
      currentUsage: current,
    };
  }

  private setHeaders(response: Response, result: any, options: RateLimitOptions): void {
    if (options.standardHeaders !== false) {
      // Standard rate limit headers (draft RFC)
      response.setHeader('RateLimit-Limit', options.limit || options.capacity);
      response.setHeader('RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining || 0);
      response.setHeader('RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime);
      
      if (result.retryAfter) {
        response.setHeader('Retry-After', result.retryAfter);
      }
    }

    if (options.legacyHeaders) {
      // Legacy X-RateLimit headers for compatibility
      response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Limit', options.limit || options.capacity);
      response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Remaining', result.remaining || 0);
      response.setHeader('X-RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime);
    }
  }
}

Microservice-Aware Rate Limiting​

Implement service-specific rate limiting strategies that work across distributed systems.

// services/distributed-rate-limit.service.ts
import { Injectable, Inject } from '@nestjs/common';
import { ClientProxy } from '@nestjs/microservices';
import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis';

interface ServiceRateLimitConfig {
  serviceName: string;
  globalLimit: number;
  perInstanceLimit: number;
  windowMs: number;
  coordinationStrategy: 'redis' | 'gossip' | 'leader-election';
}

@Injectable()
export class DistributedRateLimitService {
  private instanceId: string;
  
  constructor(
    private readonly redis: RedisService,
    @Inject('MESSAGE_BROKER') private readonly messageBroker: ClientProxy
  ) {
    this.instanceId = `${process.env.POD_NAME || 'local'}-${Date.now()}`;
  }

  async checkServiceRateLimit(
    config: ServiceRateLimitConfig,
    clientKey: string
  ): Promise<{
    allowed: boolean;
    globalUsage: number;
    instanceUsage: number;
    recommendation: 'allow' | 'deny' | 'throttle';
  }> {
    const script = `
      local globalKey = KEYS[1]
      local instanceKey = KEYS[2]
      local globalLimit = tonumber(ARGV[1])
      local perInstanceLimit = tonumber(ARGV[2])
      local windowMs = tonumber(ARGV[3])
      local now = tonumber(ARGV[4])
      local instanceId = ARGV[5]
      
      -- Clean expired entries
      local cutoff = now - windowMs
      redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', globalKey, 0, cutoff)
      redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', instanceKey, 0, cutoff)
      
      -- Get current usage
      local globalUsage = redis.call('ZCARD', globalKey)
      local instanceUsage = redis.call('ZCARD', instanceKey)
      
      -- Calculate available capacity
      local globalAvailable = globalLimit - globalUsage
      local instanceAvailable = perInstanceLimit - instanceUsage
      
      -- Determine if request should be allowed
      local allowed = globalAvailable > 0 and instanceAvailable > 0
      local recommendation = 'allow'
      
      if not allowed then
        recommendation = 'deny'
      elseif globalAvailable < globalLimit * 0.1 then
        recommendation = 'throttle'
      end
      
      if allowed then
        -- Record the request
        local requestId = instanceId .. ':' .. now .. ':' .. math.random(1000000)
        redis.call('ZADD', globalKey, now, requestId)
        redis.call('ZADD', instanceKey, now, requestId)
        redis.call('EXPIRE', globalKey, math.ceil(windowMs / 1000) * 2)
        redis.call('EXPIRE', instanceKey, math.ceil(windowMs / 1000) * 2)
        
        globalUsage = globalUsage + 1
        instanceUsage = instanceUsage + 1
      end
      
      return {
        allowed and 1 or 0,
        globalUsage,
        instanceUsage,
        recommendation
      }
    `;

    const now = Date.now();
    const globalKey = `service_rate_limit:${config.serviceName}:global:${clientKey}`;
    const instanceKey = `service_rate_limit:${config.serviceName}:${this.instanceId}:${clientKey}`;

    const result = await this.redis.eval(
      script,
      2,
      globalKey,
      instanceKey,
      config.globalLimit,
      config.perInstanceLimit,
      config.windowMs,
      now,
      this.instanceId
    ) as [number, number, number, string];

    // Publish metrics for monitoring
    await this.publishMetrics(config.serviceName, {
      globalUsage: result[1],
      instanceUsage: result[2],
      recommendation: result[3],
      timestamp: now,
    });

    return {
      allowed: result[0] === 1,
      globalUsage: result[1],
      instanceUsage: result[2],
      recommendation: result[3] as any,
    };
  }

  private async publishMetrics(serviceName: string, metrics: any): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.messageBroker.emit('rate_limit.metrics', {
        serviceName,
        instanceId: this.instanceId,
        ...metrics,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      // Metrics publishing failure shouldn't affect rate limiting
      console.warn('Failed to publish rate limit metrics:', error);
    }
  }

  async getServiceHealth(serviceName: string): Promise<{
    totalInstances: number;
    healthyInstances: number;
    globalUsage: number;
    averageInstanceUsage: number;
  }> {
    const healthKey = `service_health:${serviceName}`;
    const instances = await this.redis.hgetall(healthKey);
    
    const now = Date.now();
    const healthyThreshold = 30000; // 30 seconds
    
    let healthyCount = 0;
    let totalUsage = 0;
    
    for (const [instanceId, lastSeen] of Object.entries(instances)) {
      if (now - parseInt(lastSeen) < healthyThreshold) {
        healthyCount++;
        
        // Get instance usage
        const usageKey = `service_rate_limit:${serviceName}:${instanceId}:*`;
        const usageKeys = await this.redis.keys(usageKey);
        for (const key of usageKeys) {
          const usage = await this.redis.zcard(key);
          totalUsage += usage;
        }
      }
    }
    
    return {
      totalInstances: Object.keys(instances).length,
      healthyInstances: healthyCount,
      globalUsage: totalUsage,
      averageInstanceUsage: healthyCount > 0 ? totalUsage / healthyCount : 0,
    };
  }
}

Middleware for Global Rate Limiting​

Implement middleware for application-wide rate limiting with exemptions.

// middleware/global-rate-limit.middleware.ts
import { Injectable, NestMiddleware, HttpException, HttpStatus } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Request, Response, NextFunction } from 'express';
import { TokenBucketService } from '../rate-limiting/token-bucket.service';

@Injectable()
export class GlobalRateLimitMiddleware implements NestMiddleware {
  constructor(private readonly tokenBucket: TokenBucketService) {}

  async use(req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) {
    // Skip rate limiting for certain paths
    const exemptPaths = [
      '/health',
      '/metrics',
      '/api/v1/internal',
    ];

    if (exemptPaths.some(path => req.path.startsWith(path))) {
      return next();
    }

    // Skip for internal service calls
    if (req.headers['x-service-token'] === process.env.INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN) {
      return next();
    }

    // Apply global rate limiting
    const clientKey = this.generateClientKey(req);
    const result = await this.tokenBucket.checkRateLimit(clientKey, {
      capacity: 10000,     // 10k requests
      refillRate: 100,     // 100 requests per second
      windowSize: 3600,    // 1 hour window
    });

    // Set rate limit headers
    res.setHeader('X-Global-RateLimit-Limit', '10000');
    res.setHeader('X-Global-RateLimit-Remaining', result.remainingTokens);
    res.setHeader('X-Global-RateLimit-Reset', result.resetTime);

    if (!result.allowed) {
      throw new HttpException(
        {
          statusCode: HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
          message: 'Global rate limit exceeded',
          error: 'Too Many Requests',
          retryAfter: result.retryAfter,
        },
        HttpStatus.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
      );
    }

    next();
  }

  private generateClientKey(req: Request): string {
    // Prioritize API key, then user ID, then IP
    const apiKey = req.headers['x-api-key'] as string;
    const userId = (req as any).user?.id;
    const ip = req.ip || req.connection.remoteAddress;

    if (apiKey) {
      return `global:api:${apiKey}`;
    }
    if (userId) {
      return `global:user:${userId}`;
    }
    return `global:ip:${ip}`;
  }
}

Monitoring and Observability​

Implement comprehensive monitoring for rate limiting performance.

// monitoring/rate-limit-metrics.service.ts
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { Gauge, Counter, Histogram, register } from 'prom-client';

@Injectable()
export class RateLimitMetricsService {
  private readonly requestsTotal: Counter<string>;
  private readonly requestsBlocked: Counter<string>;
  private readonly rateLimitUsage: Gauge<string>;
  private readonly rateLimitLatency: Histogram<string>;

  constructor() {
    this.requestsTotal = new Counter({
      name: 'rate_limit_requests_total',
      help: 'Total number of requests processed by rate limiter',
      labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm', 'key_type'],
      registers: [register],
    });

    this.requestsBlocked = new Counter({
      name: 'rate_limit_requests_blocked_total',
      help: 'Total number of requests blocked by rate limiter',
      labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm', 'key_type', 'reason'],
      registers: [register],
    });

    this.rateLimitUsage = new Gauge({
      name: 'rate_limit_usage_ratio',
      help: 'Current usage ratio of rate limits (0-1)',
      labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm', 'key_type'],
      registers: [register],
    });

    this.rateLimitLatency = new Histogram({
      name: 'rate_limit_check_duration_seconds',
      help: 'Time spent checking rate limits',
      labelNames: ['service', 'algorithm'],
      buckets: [0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0],
      registers: [register],
    });
  }

  recordRequest(service: string, algorithm: string, keyType: string): void {
    this.requestsTotal.inc({ service, algorithm, key_type: keyType });
  }

  recordBlocked(
    service: string, 
    algorithm: string, 
    keyType: string, 
    reason: string
  ): void {
    this.requestsBlocked.inc({ service, algorithm, key_type: keyType, reason });
  }

  recordUsage(
    service: string, 
    algorithm: string, 
    keyType: string, 
    ratio: number
  ): void {
    this.rateLimitUsage.set({ service, algorithm, key_type: keyType }, ratio);
  }

  recordLatency(service: string, algorithm: string, duration: number): void {
    this.rateLimitLatency.observe({ service, algorithm }, duration);
  }

  async getMetrics(): Promise<string> {
    return register.metrics();
  }
}

// Health check for rate limiting system
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import { HealthIndicator, HealthIndicatorResult, HealthCheckError } from '@nestjs/terminus';
import { RedisService } from '@nestjs-modules/ioredis';

@Injectable()
export class RateLimitHealthIndicator extends HealthIndicator {
  constructor(private readonly redis: RedisService) {
    super();
  }

  async isHealthy(key: string): Promise<HealthIndicatorResult> {
    try {
      // Test Redis connectivity
      const start = Date.now();
      await this.redis.ping();
      const latency = Date.now() - start;

      // Test rate limiting functionality
      const testKey = `health_check:${Date.now()}`;
      await this.redis.incr(testKey);
      await this.redis.expire(testKey, 60);

      const isHealthy = latency < 100; // Consider healthy if latency < 100ms

      const result = this.getStatus(key, isHealthy, {
        redis_latency: latency,
        redis_status: 'connected',
      });

      if (isHealthy) {
        return result;
      }

      throw new HealthCheckError('Rate limiting is unhealthy', result);
    } catch (error) {
      throw new HealthCheckError('Rate limiting check failed', {
        [key]: {
          status: 'down',
          error: error.message,
        },
      });
    }
  }
}

        .send({ email: 'test@example.com', password: 'password' })

Best Practices and Production Considerations​

🔧 Configuration Management​

  1. Environment-Specific Limits: Use different rate limits for development, staging, and production
  2. Dynamic Configuration: Allow runtime adjustment of rate limits without deployment
  3. Graceful Degradation: Fall back to in-memory limiting if Redis is unavailable
  4. Circuit Breakers: Implement circuit breakers for rate limiting services

📊 Monitoring and Alerting​

  1. Metrics Collection: Track rate limit usage, blocked requests, and system health
  2. Alerting: Set up alerts for high block rates or system failures
  3. Dashboard: Create monitoring dashboards for real-time rate limit visibility
  4. Log Analysis: Analyze logs to identify patterns and potential abuse

⚡ Performance Optimization​

  1. Redis Optimization: Use Redis clusters for high availability and performance
  2. Lua Scripts: Leverage atomic Lua scripts for consistent rate limiting
  3. Connection Pooling: Optimize Redis connection management
  4. Caching: Cache rate limit decisions for frequently accessed keys

🛡️ Security Considerations​

  1. Key Generation: Use secure, unpredictable key generation strategies
  2. API Key Management: Implement proper API key validation and rotation
  3. Bypass Protection: Secure internal service communication channels
  4. Audit Logging: Log all rate limit decisions for security auditing

Conclusion​

Implementing robust rate limiting in NestJS microservices requires careful consideration of algorithms, distribution strategies, and production requirements. The solutions presented here provide:

  • Multiple Rate Limiting Algorithms: Token bucket, sliding window, and fixed window implementations
  • Distributed Coordination: Service-aware rate limiting across multiple instances
  • Flexible Configuration: Decorator-based and middleware approaches for different use cases
  • Production Readiness: Monitoring, health checks, and comprehensive testing
  • Performance Optimization: Redis-based storage with efficient Lua scripts

Start with simple rate limiting for critical endpoints, gradually expanding to more sophisticated distributed strategies as your microservice architecture grows. Always monitor rate limiting effectiveness and adjust limits based on actual usage patterns and business requirements.

Remember that rate limiting is just one part of a comprehensive security and performance strategy. Combine it with other techniques like authentication, authorization, caching, and circuit breakers for maximum effectiveness in production environments.
